questions.question: The statement 'Most of the major Peninsular rivers flow from west to east' is an EXCEPTION for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada and Tapi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The general slope of the **Peninsular Plateau** is from **west to east**, which is why most major rivers like the **Godavari**, **Krishna**, **Kaveri**, and **Mahanadi** flow towards the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Narmada** and **Tapi** are the two major **Peninsular rivers** that flow from **east to west**, making them the primary exceptions to the general drainage pattern. Hence, statement 4 is correct.
 
• The **Godavari** and **Krishna** rivers originate in the **Western Ghats** and flow **eastwards** into the **Bay of Bengal** following the natural gradient of the plateau. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect as an exception.
 
• The **Kaveri** and **Krishna** rivers also follow the **west-to-east** direction and form large deltas on the eastern coast of **India**. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect as an exception.
 
• The **Mahanadi** originates in the highlands of **Chhattisgarh** and the **Kaveri** in the **Brahmagiri range**; both flow **eastwards**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect as an exception.
 
• The reason **Narmada** and **Tapi** flow westwards is that they flow through **Rift Valleys** formed by faulting between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges, which divert them towards the **Arabian Sea**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Narmada River:**

 
 
• It rises in the **Amarkantak** hills in **Madhya Pradesh** at an elevation of about **1,057 meters**.
 
• It flows for a total length of **1,312 km** before joining the **Arabian Sea** in the **Gulf of Khambhat**.
 
• It creates a notable marble gorge near **Jabalpur** and the **Dhuandhar Falls**.
 
• The **Sardar Sarovar Dam** is built on this river in the state of **Gujarat**.
 
 
 
• **The Tapi River:**
 
 
• It originates in the **Satpura ranges**, in the **Betul** district of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It flows nearly parallel to the **Narmada** but is much shorter in length, measuring approximately **724 km**.
 
• Its basin covers parts of **Madhya Pradesh**, **Gujarat**, and **Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **East Flowing Rivers (The General Trend):**
 
 
• **Godavari:** It is the largest **Peninsular river** system, often referred to as the **Dakshin Ganga**. It has a length of **1,465 km** and its catchment area is the largest in **India** after the **Ganga**.
 
• **Krishna:** Rising from a spring near **Mahabaleshwar**, it flows for **1,400 km**. Major tributaries include the **Tungabhadra**, **Koyana**, and **Musie**.
 
• **Mahanadi:** It flows through **Odisha** to reach the **Bay of Bengal** with a length of about **860 km**. The **Hirakud Dam** is a major project on this river.
 
• **Kaveri:** It rises in the **Brahmagiri range** of the **Western Ghats** and reaches the **Bay of Bengal** in **Puducherry**. Its length is **800 km**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rift Valley Formation:** The **Narmada** and **Tapi** do not form deltas because of the high gradient and the hard rocky terrain they flow through; instead, they form **Estuaries**.
 
• **Luni River:** Another exception in the **Peninsular** region is the **Luni** river in **Rajasthan**, which is the largest river in the **Thar Desert** and ends in the **Rann of Kutch**, making it an **endorheic** (inland drainage) river.
 
• **Mahi River:** This is a unique river in **India** that crosses the **Tropic of Cancer** (**23.5° N**) twice during its course.
 
• **Water Divide:** The **Western Ghats** act as the main water divide for the **Peninsular** rivers, separating the drainage flowing into the **Arabian Sea** from that flowing into the **Bay of Bengal**.

questions.question: What was the theme of the 16th session of the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD16) held in Geneva in October 2025?

options.text: Promoting global trade and financial stability
Advancing technology and innovation for sustainable economies
Shaping the future: Driving economic transformation for equitable, inclusive and sustainable development
Climate Action for a Sustainable Future

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaping the future: Driving economic transformation for equitable, inclusive and sustainable development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **16th session** of the **United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD16)** is scheduled to be held in **Geneva, Switzerland**, in **October 2025**. This session marks a critical juncture for global trade discussions, focusing on the needs of **developing nations** in a rapidly changing global economy.
 
• The official theme for the **UNCTAD16** conference is "**Shaping the future: Driving economic transformation for equitable, inclusive and sustainable development**." This theme emphasizes the necessity of structural changes in economies to ensure that growth benefits everyone and protects the environment. ***Hence, the option containing this theme is correct.***
 
• The conference aims to address the growing **digital divide**, the impact of **climate change** on trade, and the **debt distress** faced by many **Global South** countries. It seeks to provide a platform for **consensus-building** among **195 member states**.
 
• The session will evaluate the progress made since **UNCTAD15**, which was held in **Barbados** in **2021**, and will set the organization's work program for the next **four years**.
 
• Key focus areas include **technology transfer**, **investment facilitation**, and the **diversification of exports** for **Least Developed Countries (LDCs)** to build resilience against global shocks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About UNCTAD:**

 
 
• **UNCTAD** was established in **1964** as a permanent intergovernmental body. It is the principal organ of the **United Nations General Assembly** dealing with **trade, investment, and development** issues.
 
• Its permanent secretariat is located in **Geneva**, and it currently has **195 member states**. The organization's primary goal is to maximize the trade, investment, and development opportunities of **developing countries** and assist them in integrating into the world economy on an equitable basis.
 
• The current **Secretary-General** of UNCTAD is **Rebeca Grynspan** of **Costa Rica**, who took office in **September 2021**, becoming the first woman to lead the organization.
 
 
 
• **Major Publications and Reports:**
 
 
• UNCTAD publishes several flagship reports that serve as benchmarks for global policy, including the **World Investment Report**, the **Trade and Development Report**, and the **Least Developed Countries Report**.
 
• The **World Investment Report** focuses on **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** trends and policies, while the **Digital Economy Report** tracks the global expansion of **e-commerce** and **digital trade**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Themes:**
 
 
• **UNCTAD15 (2021)**: Held in **Bridgetown, Barbados**, with the theme "**From inequality and vulnerability to prosperity for all**." It focused on recovering from the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• **UNCTAD14 (2016)**: Held in **Nairobi, Kenya**, with the theme "**From decision to action**," emphasizing the implementation of the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Transformation:** This refers to the process of shifting resources from low-productivity activities (like subsistence agriculture) to high-productivity sectors (like **manufacturing** and **high-tech services**). **UNCTAD16** highlights this as the key to long-term prosperity.
 
• **Equitable and Inclusive Development:** This ensures that the benefits of international trade are not concentrated in a few nations or among the wealthy, but reach **marginalized communities** and **small-scale enterprises**.
 
• **Sustainable Development:** Aligning trade policies with the **Paris Agreement** and the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** is a priority, specifically addressing **carbon leakage** and **green financing**.
 
• **Intergovernmental Machinery:** UNCTAD operates through the **Trade and Development Board** and various commissions that meet between the quadrennial conferences to monitor policy implementation and provide **technical assistance** to member states.

questions.question: A shopkeeper purchased 33 dozens of articles at the rate of ₹620 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of ₹93. What percentage profit did he make?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ CP per article = 620/12

⇒ SP per article = 93

⇒ Profit per article = 93 − 620/12 = 93 − 51.67 ≈ 41.33

⇒ % Profit = (41.33 / 51.67) × 100 = 80%

**∴ Answer = 0.8**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of dozens = 33

CP per dozen = 620

SP per article = 93

**Formula:**

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total articles = 33 × 12 = 396

⇒ Total CP = 33 × 620 = 20460

⇒ Total SP = 396 × 93 = 36828

⇒ Profit = 36828 − 20460 = 16368

⇒ Profit % = (16368 / 20460) × 100 = 80%

**Final Answer: 0.8**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Dozen:** 1 dozen = 12 units

**2. Profit:** SP − CP

**3. Profit %:** (Profit/CP) × 100

**4. Shortcut:** Compare per unit instead of total

questions.question: A car runs for 10 hours and Its speed during the ith hour is i³ km per hour, where i=1,2,3...,10. The average speed of the car for the journey is _____ km per hour.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Speeds = 1³, 2³, 3³, ... , 10³

⇒ Total distance = sum of cubes = (n(n+1)/2)²

⇒ = (10×11/2)² = 55² = 3025

⇒ Time = 10 hours

⇒ Avg speed = 3025/10 = 302.5

**∴ Answer = 302.5 km/h**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed in ith hour = i³ km/h

Total time = 10 hours

**Formula:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

Sum of cubes = [n(n+1)/2]²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 1³ + 2³ + ... + 10³

⇒ = [10×11/2]² = 55² = 3025 km

⇒ Average speed = 3025 / 10 = 302.5 km/h

**Final Answer: 302.5 km/h**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Sum of Cubes:** 1³ + 2³ + ... + n³ = [n(n+1)/2]²

**2. Average Speed:** Total distance / total time

**3. Pattern:** Cubes grow rapidly → higher total

**4. Time-based Speed:** Distance each hour = speed × 1 hr

questions.question: In 2025, which country secured the third rank in the Asia Power Index, after the United States and China?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the latest **Asia Power Index**, **India** has achieved a significant milestone by securing the **3rd rank** among **27 nations** and territories.
 
• For the first time since the index's inception, **India** has surpassed **Japan**, which now occupies the **4th position** in terms of comprehensive power in the **Asia-Pacific** region.
 
• The **United States** continues to hold the **1st rank** with a score of **81.7**, while **China** remains in the **2nd rank** with a score of **72.7**.
 
• **India's** overall score reached **39.1**, reflecting a steady upward trajectory in its regional influence and resource capabilities.
 
• The ranking highlights **India's** post-pandemic economic recovery and its growing **diplomatic influence**, which has seen a notable increase in recent years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Asia Power Index:**

 
 
• The **Asia Power Index** is an annual data-driven assessment launched in **2018** by the **Lowy Institute**, an independent think tank based in **Sydney, Australia**.
 
• It measures the power of countries across **eight thematic measures**: **Economic Capability**, **Military Capability**, **Resilience**, **Future Resources**, **Economic Relationships**, **Defense Networks**, **Diplomatic Influence**, and **Cultural Influence**.
 
 
 
• **India's Strategic Strengths:**
 
 
• **India** performs exceptionally well in the **Future Resources** category, where it ranks **2nd**, trailing only behind the **United States**. This is due to its massive **demographic dividend** and projected **economic growth**.
 
• In terms of **Diplomatic Influence**, **India** has moved up to the **4th position**, reflecting its active engagement in global forums and regional leadership roles.
 
• The country is classified as a **"Major Power"**, a status reserved for nations with scores above **10** in the index.
 
 
 
• **Japan's Position:**
 
 
• **Japan** slipped to the **4th rank** with a score of **38.9**. While it remains a significant **"Smart Power"** that excels in **Economic Relationships** and **Defense Networks**, it faces challenges due to an **aging population** and **economic stagnation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regional Dynamics:** The index covers countries as far west as **Pakistan**, as far north as **Russia**, and as far into the Pacific as **Australia**, **New Zealand**, and the **United States**.
 
• **India as an "Underachiever":** Despite its **3rd rank**, the report notes that **India** is still an **"underachiever"** relative to its available resources, meaning its actual influence in the region is less than what its **population** and **geography** would suggest.
 
• **Key Rankings for 2024/2025:**
 
 
• **Rank 1: United States (81.7)**
 
• **Rank 2: China (72.7)**
 
• **Rank 3: India (39.1)**
 
• **Rank 4: Japan (38.9)**
 
• **Rank 5: Australia (31.9)**
 
 
 
• **Strategic Implications:** **India’s** rise is significantly bolstered by its membership in the **Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad)** and its expanding **military capability**, where it currently ranks **4th** globally within the index's scope.

questions.question: Which group at IIT Bombay developed the Quantum Diamond Microscope in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P-Quest Group**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Quantum Diamond Microscope (QDM)** was developed by the **P-Quest Group**, which stands for **Precision Quantum Engineering, Science and Technology**. This research group is based at the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay**.
 
• The development of this advanced imaging tool was led by **Associate Professor Kasturi Saha** from the **Department of Electrical Engineering** at **IIT Bombay**. The team unveiled this technology to enhance **India's** capabilities in quantum sensing and metrology.
 
• The **Quantum Diamond Microscope** is a high-sensitivity magnetic field imaging device that utilizes **Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) centers** in **synthetic diamonds** as quantum sensors. This allows for the mapping of magnetic fields with **micrometer-scale** spatial resolution.
 
• The project is a significant milestone under the **National Quantum Mission (NQM)**, which was approved by the **Government of India** in **2023** with a total outlay of over **Rs. 6,000 crore** to propel **India** into a leading role in quantum technology.
 
• The **P-Quest Group** at **IIT Bombay** focuses on using quantum states of light and matter for applications in **communication**, **sensing**, and **computing**. Their work on the microscope was supported by the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)** and the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technological Features:**

 
 
• The microscope operates by using a **green laser** to excite the **NV centers** in the **diamond**. As these centers return to their ground state, they emit **red fluorescence**, the intensity of which changes in response to local **magnetic fields**.
 
• It provides **non-destructive testing** capabilities, meaning it can inspect **semiconductor chips** and **electronic circuits** for defects without causing any physical damage to the components.
 
• The device can operate at **room temperature**, which is a major advantage over other quantum sensors that require **cryogenic cooling** (extremely low temperatures).
 
 
 
• **Applications and Uses:**
 
 
• **Semiconductor Industry:** It is used for **failure analysis** in integrated circuits (ICs), helping **engineers** locate **short circuits** or **current leakages** in **microchips**.
 
• **Biomedical Imaging:** The **Quantum Diamond Microscope** can be used to image **magnetic nanoparticles** within **biological cells**, aiding in advanced **medical diagnostics** and **drug delivery** research.
 
• **Geology and Material Science:** It assists in studying the **magnetic properties** of **minerals** and new **2D materials** like **graphene**.
 
 
 
• **National Quantum Mission (NQM):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2023**, the **NQM** aims to develop **intermediate-scale quantum computers** with **50-1000 physical qubits** within **eight years**.
 
• The mission is implemented by the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)** and targets four main domains: **Quantum Computing**, **Quantum Communication**, **Quantum Sensing and Metrology**, and **Quantum Materials and Devices**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) Center:** This is a **point defect** in the **diamond lattice** where a **nitrogen atom** replaces a **carbon atom**, and an adjacent site is empty (a **vacancy**). It is a key building block for **quantum sensors** due to its **electron spin** properties.
 
• **India's Strategic Position:** With the development of the **Quantum Diamond Microscope**, **India** joins a select group of **countries**, including the **USA**, **Germany**, and **Australia**, that possess indigenous capabilities in **quantum imaging**.
 
• **Location of Development:** The research was conducted at the **IIT Bombay** campus in **Powai, Mumbai**. The institute is one of the premier **Technical Universities** in **India**, consistently ranked high in the **NIRF** and **QS World University Rankings**.
 
• **Date and Year:** The formal announcement and successful demonstration of the **prototype** were highlighted in **late 2024** and early **2025**, marking a new era for **deep-tech startups** in the **Indian** ecosystem.

questions.question: Piyush bought an article for ₹331 and sold it to Payal at a loss of 5%. With this amount, Piyush bought another article and sold it at a gain of 60%. What is Piyush's overall gain percentage?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Net effect = (1 − 5/100) × (1 + 60/100)

⇒ = 0.95 × 1.6 = 1.52

⇒ Gain = 52%

**∴ Answer = 0.52**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

CP = 331

Loss = 5%

Gain = 60%

**Formula:**

SP = CP × (1 ± %/100)

SP₁ = 331 × 0.95 = 314.45

⇒ Second sale (60% gain):

SP₂ = 314.45 × 1.6 = 503.12

⇒ Net gain = 503.12 − 331 = 172.12

⇒ Gain % = (172.12 / 331) × 100 = 52%

**Final Answer: 0.52**

**1. Successive Change:** Multiply factors directly

**2. Loss/Gain Factor:** Loss → (1 − x/100), Gain → (1 + x/100)

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties is associated with the Thousand Pillars Temple at Warangal built in the 12th century?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kakatiya dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Thousand Pillar Temple**, also known as the **Rudreshwara Swamy Temple**, is a historic Hindu temple located in **Hanamkonda** town near **Warangal** in the state of **Telangana**, **India**.
 
• It was constructed in the year **1163 AD** during the reign of the **Kakatiya dynasty**. The construction was commissioned by the ruler **King Rudra Deva**. *Hence, the statement regarding its association with the Kakatiya dynasty is correct.*
 
• The temple is a classic example of **Kakatiya architecture**, which reached its zenith during the **12th century**. It is built in the **Vesara** style and is famous for its intricate carvings and perforated stone screens.
 
• It is a **Trikutalaya**, which means it consists of three shrines dedicated to three different deities: **Lord Shiva**, **Lord Vishnu**, and **Lord Surya** (the Sun God). *Hence, the statement about it being a triple shrine is correct.*
 
• The temple is supported by **one thousand pillars**, which are intricately carved but positioned in a way that they never obstruct the view of the deities from any point in the temple.
 
• A massive monolithic **Nandi** (the sacred bull of Shiva) carved out of a single **black basalt** stone is placed at the entrance, reflecting the artistic brilliance of the **Kakatiya** era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kakatiya Dynasty (1083–1323 AD):**

 
 
• This dynasty ruled the eastern **Deccan** region, comprising modern-day **Telangana** and **Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• Their capital was initially **Hanamkonda** and later shifted to **Orugallu** (modern **Warangal**).
 
• Notable rulers include **Ganapati Deva**, **Rani Rudrama Devi**, and **Prataparudra**. They were known for constructing massive irrigation tanks and grand temples like the **Ramappa Temple** (a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**).
 
 
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty (753–982 AD):**
 
 
• They ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent between the **8th and 10th centuries**.
 
• Their most famous architectural achievement is the **Kailasa Temple** at **Ellora** (Maharashtra), which is a rock-cut monolithic structure.
 
 
 
• **Hoysala Dynasty (1006–1346 AD):**
 
 
• Based in modern-day **Karnataka**, the Hoysalas are famous for their unique **star-shaped** temple plans.
 
• Major examples of their work include the **Hoysaleswara Temple** at **Halebidu** and the **Chennakesava Temple** at **Belur**, built primarily in the **12th and 13th centuries**.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**
 
 
• The **Badami Chalukyas** (6th-8th century) and the **Western Chalukyas of Kalyani** (10th-12th century) were major powers in the Deccan.
 
• They were pioneers of the **Vesara** style of architecture, with significant sites located in **Aihole**, **Badami**, and **Pattadakal**.

• **Historical Significance:** The temple was desecrated during the invasion of the **Deccan** by the **Delhi Sultanate** (led by **Alauddin Khilji** and later **Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq**) in the **14th century**.
 
• **Cultural Impact:** The **Kakatiyas** promoted the **Telugu** language and **Shaivism**. The Thousand Pillar Temple remains a primary pilgrimage and tourist destination in **South India**, showcasing the **medieval** engineering marvels of the region.

questions.question: Which of the following programs aims at self-employment for the rural poor?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)** is a flagship program launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development** in **June 2011**. It was originally launched as **Aajeevika - National Rural Livelihoods Mission** and later renamed in **2015**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• The primary objective of the program is to alleviate **rural poverty** by creating efficient and effective institutional platforms for the **rural poor**, enabling them to increase **household income** through sustainable **livelihood enhancements** and improved access to **financial services**.
 
• It focuses on promoting **self-employment** and **organization** of the rural poor into **Self Help Groups (SHGs)**. This helps in building the **capacities** of the poor and providing them with **skills** and **financial resources** to start their own **micro-enterprises**.
 
• The **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** is designed to provide **guaranteed wage employment** for at least **100 days** in a financial year to **unskilled manual laborers**; it is not primarily a **self-employment** scheme. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• The **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)** was launched in **April 2005** to provide accessible, affordable, and quality **healthcare** to the **rural population**, particularly the vulnerable sections. It does not focus on **self-employment**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, specifically the **Gramin (Rural)** component launched in **2016**, aims to provide **pucca houses** with basic amenities to all **houseless householders** and those living in **kutcha houses**. It is a **housing scheme**, not a **self-employment program**. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of DAY-NRLM:** The program succeeded the **Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)**. It is supported by the **World Bank** and is one of the **world's largest initiatives** to improve the livelihoods of the **poor**. It covers **28 States** and **8 Union Territories** across **India**.
 
• **MGNREGA Features:** Enacted in **September 2005**, this **Act** provides a **legal guarantee** for work. If work is not provided within **15 days** of application, the applicant is entitled to an **unemployment allowance**. At least **one-third** of the beneficiaries must be **women**.
 
• **PMAY-Gramin Details:** The scheme targets the construction of **2.95 crore houses**. The **cost-sharing** ratio between the **Central** and **State** governments is **60:40** in plain areas and **90:10** for **North Eastern** and **Hilly States**.
 
• **NRHM Objectives:** It seeks to reduce the **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)** and **Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR)**. It introduced the **Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA)**, a trained female community health activist, to act as an interface between the community and the **public health system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Core Pillars of DAY-NRLM:** The scheme relies on **social mobilization**, **financial inclusion**, and **sustainable livelihoods**. It encourages **universal social mobilization** by ensuring at least **one woman member** from each **rural poor household** is brought into the **SHG network**.
 
• **Livelihood Diversification:** Under **DAY-NRLM**, the **poor** are encouraged to pursue **farm** (agriculture, livestock, fisheries) and **non-farm** (handicrafts, services, retail) occupations to ensure **year-round income**.
 
• **Interest Subvention:** The scheme provides **interest subvention** to **SHG members** who avail of **bank loans**, reducing the **cost of credit** and encouraging **entrepreneurship** among **rural women**.
 
• **Identification of Beneficiaries:** Unlike many schemes that use the **BPL (Below Poverty Line)** list, **DAY-NRLM** uses the **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011** data and a process called **Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP)** to identify **target households**.

questions.question: There are 45 members in group A, 31 members in group B and 48 members in group C. All the members of these groups went to a restaurant. questions.question: As per the World Economic Outlook January 2026, by the International Monetary Fund, global economic expansion in 2027, is expected to be which of the following rates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.2 percent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, in its **World Economic Outlook (WEO)** update released in **January 2026**, has projected that the **global economic expansion** for the year **2027** will be **3.2 percent**.
 
• This forecast indicates a steady growth trajectory for the global economy, maintaining a similar pace as projected for **2025** and **2026**, which also hovered around the **3.1 to 3.2 percent** mark.
 
• The **3.2 percent** growth rate for **2027** is driven by the resilient performance of **Emerging Market and Developing Economies**, which are expected to grow at a faster rate compared to **Advanced Economies**.
 
• The report suggests that the global economy has moved past the significant inflationary pressures of the early **2020s**, with **monetary policy** normalization expected to be well underway by **2027**.
 
• According to the **IMF**, the stability in growth is attributed to improved **supply-side** conditions and the continued integration of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** into the labor markets of high-income nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The International Monetary Fund (IMF):**

 
 
• The **IMF** is a major international financial institution, headquartered in **Washington, D.C.**, consisting of **190 member countries**.
 
• It was conceived in **July 1944** at the **United Nations Bretton Woods Conference** in the **United States**.
 
• The primary mission of the **IMF** is to ensure the stability of the international monetary system, including the system of **exchange rates** and **international payments**.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Outlook (WEO):**
 
 
• The **WEO** is a comprehensive report published by the **IMF** twice a year, typically in **April** and **October**, with smaller "updates" published in **January** and **July**.
 
• It provides detailed analysis and forecasts for **global growth**, **inflation**, and **trade**, serving as a key reference for policymakers and economists worldwide.
 
• The reports use **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** based on **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** weights to aggregate global and regional growth figures.
 
 
 
• **Economic Classifications:**
 
 
• **Advanced Economies:** These include the **United States**, **Euro Area**, **Japan**, and the **United Kingdom**. These regions often see lower but more stable growth rates.
 
• **Emerging Market and Developing Economies:** This group includes major players like **India** and **China**. **India** has consistently been one of the fastest-growing major economies in these reports.
 
 
 
• **Key Economic Indicators:**
 
 
• **Global Inflation:** The **IMF** tracks headline and core **inflation**. By **2027**, global headline inflation is projected to align closer to central bank targets.
 
• **Fiscal Policy:** The **WEO** often emphasizes the need for **fiscal consolidation** to manage the rising **public debt** levels across various nations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Projected Trends:** The **January 2026** update highlights that while growth is steady at **3.2 percent**, the medium-term growth prospects remain lower than the historical average of **3.8 percent** seen between **2000 and 2019**.
 
• **Risks to Forecast:** Potential risks to the **2027** expansion include **geopolitical tensions**, fluctuations in **commodity prices** (such as **crude oil**), and potential disruptions in **global supply chains**.
 
• **Managing Director:** As of the report period, the **IMF** is led by its **Managing Director**, a position held by **Kristalina Georgieva** (who started her term in **2019**).
 
• **Comparison with World Bank:** Similar to the **IMF**, the **World Bank** also releases the **Global Economic Prospects** report, though their methodologies and specific **GDP** growth numerical values may vary slightly based on different base years and calculation methods.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to States and Union Territories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fourth Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Fourth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the **allocation of seats** in the **Rajya Sabha** (the Council of States) to the various **States** and **Union Territories**. ***Hence, the first option is correct.***
 
• The allocation of these seats is determined based on the **population** of each state. Consequently, the number of representatives varies from state to state; for example, **Uttar Pradesh** has the highest representation with **31** seats, while smaller states like **Sikkim** have only **1** seat.
 
• This schedule is linked with **Article 4(1)** and **Article 80(2)** of the **Indian Constitution**, which mandate the structure and composition of the upper house of **Parliament**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** currently has a total of **245** members, although the maximum strength is fixed at **250**. Out of these, **233** members are representatives of the **States** and **Union Territories**, and **12** members are nominated by the **President** for their contributions to **art**, **literature**, **science**, and **social services**.
 
• Among the **Union Territories**, only **Delhi** (**3** seats), **Puducherry** (**1** seat), and **Jammu & Kashmir** (**4** seats) have representation in the **Rajya Sabha** because their population sizes are large enough to warrant it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Schedule**:

 
 
• This schedule contains the names of the **States** and **Union Territories** along with their **territorial jurisdiction** and extent.
 
• It currently lists **28** **States** and **8** **Union Territories** following the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019** and the merger of **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** and **Daman and Diu** in **2020**.
 
 
 
• **Second Schedule**:
 
 
• It lists the provisions relating to the **emoluments**, **allowances**, and **privileges** of high-ranking officials.
 
• This includes the **President of India**, **Governors of States**, **Speaker** and **Deputy Speaker** of the **Lok Sabha**, **Chairman** and **Deputy Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**, and **Judges** of the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Schedule**:
 
 
• It contains provisions for the administration of **tribal areas** in the four northeastern states of **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, **Tripura**, and **Mizoram**.
 
• It allows for the creation of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)** to safeguard the rights of tribal communities and manage land, forests, and local customs.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule**:
 
 
• This schedule deals with the division of powers between the **Union** and the **States** through three lists: the **Union List** (currently **100** subjects), the **State List** (currently **61** subjects), and the **Concurrent List** (currently **52** subjects).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is known as the **Permanent House** because it is not subject to **dissolution**.
 
• Members of the **Rajya Sabha** are elected for a term of **6 years**, and **one-third** of the members retire every **second year**.
 
• The election process involves the **elected members** of the **Legislative Assemblies** of the **States** and **Union Territories** using the system of **proportional representation** by means of a **single transferable vote**.
 
• The **Vice-President of India** serves as the **ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• The **Representation of the People Act, 1951** governs various aspects of the election and functioning of the members in accordance with the **Constitution**.

questions.question: Which institution formed by Pandit Birju Maharaj focuses on imparting training in the field of Kathak and related disciplines?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalashram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalashram** is the world-renowned institution founded by the **Kathak** maestro **Pandit Birju Maharaj** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The primary **focus** of this institution is to impart training in the field of **Kathak** dance, along with other associated disciplines like **Yoga**, **Painting**, **Vocal Music**, and the playing of **musical instruments**.
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj** established this institute to preserve and promote the **Kalka-Bindadin Gharana** of **Lucknow**, which is characterized by its graceful movements and intricate footwork.
 
• The institution reflects the **philosophy** of **Birju Maharaj**, which treats dance as a holistic art form integrated with spiritual and physical well-being.
 
• The training at **Kalashram** follows the traditional **Guru-Shishya Parampara**, ensuring the authentic transmission of **Kathak** techniques to future generations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj** (born **Brijmohan Nath Mishra**) was born on **4 February 1938** and passed away on **17 January 2022**. He was a legendary figure in **Indian classical dance**.
 
• He belonged to the **Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" Gharana**, a lineage that has produced some of the greatest **Kathak** dancers in **India**.
 
• **Birju Maharaj** was a multi-talented artist; besides being a dancer, he was a **singer**, **composer**, and **poet**. He was proficient in playing the **Tabla**, **Pakhawaj**, and **Dholak**.
 
• In recognition of his immense contribution to the arts, he was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan**, **India's** second-highest civilian award, in **1986**.
 
• He also served as the Head of Faculty and Director at the **Kathak Kendra** (National Institute of Kathak Dance) in **New Delhi** for many years before founding **Kalashram**.
 
• **Kathak** is one of the **eight major forms** of **Indian classical dance**. Its **origin** is attributed to the traveling storytellers of ancient **Northern India**, known as **Kathakars**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Reach:** **Pandit Birju Maharaj** took **Kathak** to the global stage, performing in numerous **countries** and establishing a worldwide following.
 
• **Choreography in Cinema:** He contributed significantly to **Indian Cinema** by choreographing iconic dance sequences in **movies** like **Shatranj Ke Khilari** (directed by **Satyajit Ray**), **Devdas**, **Bajirao Mastani**, and **Vishwaroopam**.
 
• **Awards and Honors:** Apart from the **Padma Vibhushan**, he received the **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in **1964**, the **Kalidas Samman**, and a **National Film Award** for **Best Choreography** in **2012**.
 
• **Lineage:** He was the son and disciple of **Jagannath Maharaj**, popularly known as **Acchan Maharaj**. His uncles were the famous **Lachhu Maharaj** and **Shambhu Maharaj**.
 
• **Artistic Features:** **Kathak** is distinguished by its **Chakkars** (vertical spins), **Tatkar** (footwork), and **Abhinaya** (expressional dance), all of which were mastered and taught by **Birju Maharaj** at **Kalashram**.

questions.question: In the field of e-commerce and financial trading, which application of computers is essential for analyzing massive volumes of rapidly changing market data and detecting complex patterns to inform investment decisions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Real-time Predictive Analytics**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real-time Predictive Analytics** is the use of **data**, **statistical algorithms**, and **machine learning** techniques to identify the likelihood of future outcomes based on historical and current **data**. In **e-commerce** and **finance**, it is essential for processing **big data** at high speeds.
 
• In the context of **financial trading**, these systems analyze **massive volumes** of rapidly changing **market data**, including **stock prices**, **currency fluctuations**, and **trading volumes**, to execute trades in **milliseconds**.
 
• The primary **function** of this technology is to detect **complex patterns** and **market trends** that are invisible to human analysts, allowing institutional investors to make informed **investment decisions** and manage **risk** effectively.
 
• In **e-commerce**, **Predictive Analytics** is used for **dynamic pricing**, where prices of products change in **real-time** based on **consumer demand**, **competitor pricing**, and **inventory levels**.
 
• This technology relies on **high-performance computing** and **cloud-based infrastructures** to ensure that **data processing** happens with minimal **latency**, which is critical for **high-frequency trading (HFT)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Data Encryption and Security Software**: This involves **cryptographic protocols** like **AES-256** or **SSL/TLS** to protect **financial transactions** and **user data** from **cyber threats**. While critical for **trust** in **e-commerce**, its **application** is **security**, not **market analysis**.
 
• **Inventory Management Systems**: These are **software applications** used by **retailers** to track **stock levels**, **orders**, **sales**, and **deliveries**. questions.question: Which of the following types of weathering is primarily responsible for the formation of karst landscapes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical weathering**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chemical weathering** is the fundamental process responsible for the development of **karst landscapes**. This type of weathering involves the **chemical transformation** of rock minerals into new compounds, often leading to the **dissolution** of the rock. *Hence, the statement regarding chemical weathering being the primary cause is correct.*
 
• The specific chemical process involved is **carbonation**. When **rainwater** passes through the **atmosphere** and **soil**, it absorbs **carbon dioxide** (**CO2**), forming a weak solution of **carbonic acid**.
 
• This acidic water reacts with **soluble rocks**, most notably **limestone** (which is composed of **calcium carbonate**), **dolomite**, and **gypsum**. The reaction converts **insoluble calcium carbonate** into **soluble calcium bicarbonate**, which is then carried away in solution.
 
• As the rock dissolves over **thousands of years**, it creates unique surface and sub-surface features such as **sinkholes** (also known as **dolines**), **caves**, **caverns**, and **disappearing streams**.
 
• The formation of **karst** requires specific conditions: the presence of **highly jointed**, **dense**, and **thinly bedded** soluble rocks near the surface, along with **moderate to heavy rainfall** to sustain the dissolution process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mechanical Weathering**: Also known as **physical weathering**, it refers to the **physical disintegration** of rocks into smaller fragments without any change in their chemical makeup. Common processes include **frost wedging**, **abrasion**, and **pressure release**. While it breaks down rocks, it does not produce the **dissolution features** seen in karst. *Hence, the statement regarding mechanical weathering forming karst is incorrect.*
 
• **Biological Weathering**: This is the breakdown of rocks caused by **living organisms**. For example, **plant roots** may grow into cracks and exert pressure, or **lichens** and **bacteria** may produce organic acids that slowly corrode minerals. It often acts in tandem with chemical weathering but is not the **primary architect** of karst. *Hence, the statement regarding biological weathering as the primary cause is incorrect.*
 
• **Thermal Weathering**: This occurs due to **expansion and contraction** of rock minerals resulting from **temperature fluctuations**. It is most prevalent in **arid and desert regions** where the **diurnal temperature range** is high. *Hence, the statement regarding thermal weathering forming karst is incorrect.*
 
• **Geographic Distribution**: Famous **karst regions** include the **Karst Plateau** in **Slovenia** (from which the name originates), the **Yucatán Peninsula** in **Mexico**, and the **Ha Long Bay** in **Vietnam**. In **India**, karst features are prominent in the **Bastar district** of **Chhattisgarh** (**Kotumsar caves**) and parts of the **Himalayas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Speleothems**: These are **mineral deposits** formed in caves as a result of **chemical precipitation**. The most common are **stalactites** (hanging from the ceiling), **stalagmites** (rising from the floor), and **pillars** (formed when the two meet).
 
• **Uvalas and Poljes**: In advanced stages of **karst topography**, individual **sinkholes** may coalesce to form larger depressions called **uvalas**. Extremely large, flat-bottomed depressions are known as **poljes**, which can cover several **square kilometers**.
 
• **Hydrogeology**: **Karst aquifers** are vital sources of **groundwater**, providing water for **millions of people** worldwide. However, they are highly **vulnerable to pollution** because surface water can enter the underground system rapidly through **sinkholes** without significant filtration.
 
• **Climate Influence**: **Chemical weathering** is significantly more effective in **hot and humid climates**. The rate of **rock dissolution** increases with higher **temperatures** and greater **water availability**.

questions.question: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), what is the premium rate paid by farmers for annual commercial and horticultural crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5% of the sum insured**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)** was launched on **18th February 2016** by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** to provide financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen events.
 
• Under this scheme, there is a uniform premium of only **2%** to be paid by farmers for all **Kharif crops**. This is the standard rate for food crops and oilseeds during the monsoon season.
 
• For all **Rabi crops**, the premium to be paid by the farmers is **1.5%**. This lower rate is applicable for the winter cropping season.
 
• In the case of **annual commercial and annual horticultural crops**, the premium to be paid by farmers is **5% of the sum insured**. Hence, the statement regarding the 5% rate for commercial crops is **correct**.
 
• The **balance premium** (the difference between the actual premium rate and the rate paid by farmers) is paid by the **Government** (shared equally by the **Central** and **State Governments**) to provide the full insured amount to the farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of PMFBY**:

 
 
• To provide **insurance coverage** and financial support to the farmers in the event of failure of any of the notified crops as a result of **natural calamities**, **pests**, and **diseases**.
 
• To **stabilize the income** of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming.
 
• To encourage farmers to adopt **innovative and modern agricultural practices**.
 
• To ensure the **flow of credit** to the agriculture sector.
 
 
 
• **Scheme Administration**:
 
 
• The scheme is administered by the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**, Government of India.
 
• It replaced the **National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS)** and the **Modified National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (MNAIS)** to remove their inherent drawbacks.
 
 
 
• **Coverage and Scope**:
 
 
• The scheme covers **Yield Losses** (standing crops), **Prevented Sowing/Planting**, and **Post-Harvest Losses** (up to a maximum period of **14 days** from harvesting).
 
• It also includes **Localized Calamities** such as hailstorms, landslides, and inundation affecting isolated farms in the notified area.
 
• Since **Kharif 2020**, the scheme has been made **voluntary** for all farmers, whereas earlier it was compulsory for **loanee farmers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technology Integration**: The scheme promotes the use of **modern technology** like **Smartphones** for capturing and uploading data of crop cutting to reduce the delay in claim payment to farmers. **Remote Sensing** and **Drones** are also utilized for estimation of crop losses.
 
• **Premium Subsidy Sharing**: The **Central Government** and **State Governments** share the premium subsidy on a **50:50** basis, except for the **North-Eastern States**, where the sharing ratio is **90:10** (since 2020) to encourage higher penetration in these regions.
 
• **Exclusions**: Risks like **war**, **nuclear risks**, **malicious damage**, and other preventable risks are generally excluded from the insurance coverage.
 
• **Implementation Agency**: PMFBY is implemented by the **Agriculture Insurance Company of India (AIC)** and several private insurance companies empanelled by the government based on **competitive bidding**.
 
• **Numerical Data**: Since its inception, the scheme has covered over **30 crore farmer applications** and has paid out claims worth billions of rupees, significantly improving the **social security** net for the Indian farming community.

questions.question: Which leader famously declared 'Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it' during the Extremist Phase of the Indian National Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was the leader who famously declared **"Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"** in **1916**. This slogan became a rallying cry for millions of Indians during the struggle for independence. ***Hence, the first option is correct.***
 
• He was a prominent figure in the **Extremist Phase** (**1905-1919**) of the **Indian National Movement**. Unlike the Moderates, Tilak advocated for **self-rule (Swaraj)** rather than mere constitutional reforms.
 
• Tilak earned the title **"Lokmanya"**, which translates to "accepted by the people as their leader". The British colonial authorities referred to him as the **"Father of Indian Unrest"**, a term coined by **Valentine Chirol**.
 
• He utilized journalism as a tool for political education, publishing two newspapers: **Kesari** in **Marathi** and **The Mahratta** in **English**. Through these, he criticized the **British Government** and spread nationalist ideas.
 
• To bridge the gap between the masses and the political movement, he popularized the **Ganpati Festival** in **1893** and the **Shivaji Festival** in **1895** in **Maharashtra**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal:** Known as the **"Father of Revolutionary Thoughts in India"**, he was a key part of the **Lal-Bal-Pal** triumvirate. He played a major role in the **Swadeshi Movement** following the **Partition of Bengal** in **1905** and advocated for the **boycott** of British goods. ***Hence, the second option is incorrect.***
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:** Popularly known as **"Punjab Kesari"** or the **"Lion of Punjab"**, he was another pillar of the **Extremist** faction. He founded the **Punjab National Bank** and was a leading figure in the protest against the **Simon Commission** in **1928**, where he suffered fatal injuries during a **lathi charge**. ***Hence, the fourth option is incorrect.***
 
• **Aurobindo Ghose:** An intellectual leader of the **Extremist Phase**, he emphasized the concept of **Passive Resistance**. He later retired from active politics and moved to **Pondicherry** to focus on spirituality and yoga, writing famous works like **"The Life Divine"** and **"Savitri"**. ***Hence, the third option is incorrect.***
 
• **Extremist Phase (1905-1919):** This period marked a shift from the **Moderates'** policy of "Prayers, Petitions, and Protests" to more radical methods including **Swadeshi**, **Boycott**, and **National Education**. The **Surat Split** of **1907** saw the formal separation of the **Moderates** and **Extremists** within the **Indian National Congress**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Home Rule Movement:** In **April 1916**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** launched the **Indian Home Rule League** at **Belgaum**. He worked alongside **Annie Besant** to demand **Self-Government** for India within the **British Empire**.
 
• **Lucknow Pact:** Tilak played a crucial role in the **1916 Lucknow Session**, where he was instrumental in the **Lucknow Pact** between the **Indian National Congress** and the **Muslim League**, as well as the reunion of **Moderates** and **Extremists**.
 
• **Literary Works:** While serving a **six-year prison term** in **Mandalay (Burma)** from **1908 to 1914**, Tilak wrote **"Gita Rahasya"**, an interpretation of the **Bhagavad Gita** focused on **Karma Yoga** (the path of action). He also authored **"The Arctic Home in the Vedas"**, where he proposed a theory about the origin of the **Aryans**.

Solve the system of equations below for X, Y and Z:

X + 2Y + 4Z = 12

2X + 2Y + 3Z = 10

3X + 2Y + Z = 8

Subtract (3)−(2): X − 2Z = −2

⇒ Subtract both ⇒ Z = 0

⇒ Then X = −2

⇒ Put in (1): Y = 7

**∴ Answer: X = −2, Y = 7, Z = 0**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

X + 2Y + 4Z = 12

Elimination method

⇒ X − Z = −2

⇒ (3X + 2Y + Z) − (2X + 2Y + 3Z) = 8 − 10

⇒ X − 2Z = −2

⇒ (X − Z) − (X − 2Z) = −2 − (−2)

⇒ Z = 0

⇒ X − Z = −2

⇒ X = −2

⇒ X + 2Y + 4Z = 12

⇒ −2 + 2Y + 0 = 12

⇒ 2Y = 14

⇒ Y = 7

**∴ The correct answer is X = −2, Y = 7, Z = 0.**

**Tip:** Reduce system to 2 variables first, then solve

questions.question: The HCF of two numbers is 104 and their LCM is 1040. If one of the numbers is 208, what is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Second Number = (HCF × LCM) ÷ First Number

Second Number = (104 × 1040) ÷ 208

As 208 = 104 × 2, Second Number = 1040 ÷ 2 = 520

Sum = 208 + 520 = 728

**∴ Answer = 728**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

HCF of two numbers = 104

LCM of two numbers = 1040

One of the numbers (a) = 208

**Formula used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

Sum of numbers = a + b

 Num 1: 208 + Num 2: 520 
• 
 Sum = 728 Product Relation: 208 × 520 = 104 × 1040 

**Calculations:**

Let the second number be b.

⇒ 208 × b = 104 × 1040

⇒ b = (104 × 1040) ÷ 208

⇒ b = 108160 ÷ 208

⇒ b = 520

⇒ Sum = 208 + 520 = 728

**∴ The correct answer is 728.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Property

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators) and LCM = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime, their HCF is 1 and their LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.

Factor Property

The HCF of a group of numbers is always a factor of their LCM. If HCF does not divide LCM, such a set of numbers cannot exist.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates the provision of humane working conditions and maternity relief?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 42**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 42** of the **Constitution of India** specifically mandates that the **State** shall make provisions for securing **just and humane conditions of work** and for **maternity relief**.
 
• This article is a part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are contained in **Part IV** of the **Constitution**, spanning from **Article 36 to Article 51**.
 
• The primary objective of **Article 42** is to ensure that the **working environment** for employees is safe, healthy, and respectful of human dignity, while also providing necessary support to **women workers** during and after **pregnancy**.
 
• It reflects the **Socialist Principles** of the **Indian Constitution**, aiming to bridge the gap between the **capital** and **labor** by protecting the welfare of the workforce.
 
• The **State** is expected to apply these principles while making **laws** and **policies**, although they are **non-justiciable** in a court of law, meaning they cannot be legally enforced like **Fundamental Rights**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 41:** This article provides for the **right to work**, to **education**, and to **public assistance** in certain cases such as **unemployment**, **old age**, **sickness**, and **disablement**. It ensures that the **State**, within the limits of its economic capacity, makes effective provisions for these rights.
 
• **Article 44:** This article directs the **State** to endeavor to secure for the citizens a **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)** throughout the **territory of India**. questions.question: The Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh was constitutionalized through which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One Hundredth Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **One Hundredth Amendment Act, 2015** of the **Constitution of India** was enacted to give effect to the acquiring of certain territories by **India** and the transfer of certain other territories to **Bangladesh**. This was done in pursuance of the **Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) of 1974** and its **Protocol of 2011**. ***Hence, the option regarding the One Hundredth Amendment is correct.***
 
• Through this amendment, **India** transferred **111 enclaves** (covering approximately **17,160 acres**) to **Bangladesh**, while **Bangladesh** transferred **51 enclaves** (covering approximately **7,110 acres**) to **India**. This exchange of **enclaves** (also known as **Chitmahals**) resolved a decades-old border dispute.
 
• The amendment modified the **First Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**, which defines the **territorial extent** of the states and union territories. The changes specifically impacted the territories of four **Indian states**: **West Bengal**, **Assam**, **Meghalaya**, and **Tripura**.
 
• The **Land Boundary Agreement** was originally signed on **May 16, 1974**, by Prime Ministers **Indira Gandhi** and **Sheikh Mujibur Rahman**. However, it required a **constitutional amendment** in India because the **Supreme Court** had ruled in the **Berubari Union case (1960)** that any cession of **Indian territory** to a foreign nation requires an amendment under **Article 368**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ninety-Seventh Amendment (2011)**:

 
 
• This amendment gave **constitutional status** and protection to **co-operative societies**.
 
• It made the **right to form co-operative societies** a **fundamental right** under **Article 19(1)(c)**.
 
• It inserted a new **Directive Principle of State Policy** (**Article 43B**) for the promotion of **co-operative societies** and added **Part IXB** to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Ninety-Eighth Amendment (2012)**:
 
 
• It provided for **special provisions** for the **Hyderabad-Karnataka region** of the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• It inserted **Article 371J** to empower the **Governor of Karnataka** to take steps for the development of this backward region, including the creation of a separate **development board** and **equitable allocation of funds**.
 
 
 
• **One Hundred and First Amendment (2016)**:
 
 
• This amendment paved the way for the introduction of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** in India.
 
• It replaced various **indirect taxes** levied by the **Central** and **State Governments** with a single unified tax system to create a **common national market**.
 
• It led to the insertion of **Articles 246A, 269A, and 279A** (relating to the **GST Council**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Humanitarian Aspect**: The **100th Amendment** was significant not just for **geopolitics** but for **human rights**. Around **51,000 residents** living in these **enclaves** were previously "stateless" and lacked access to basic **government services**. Post-amendment, they were given the choice of **citizenship** in either **India** or **Bangladesh**.
 
• **Un-demarcated Boundary**: Besides the exchange of **enclaves**, the agreement also settled the **demarcation** of a **6.1-kilometer** un-demarcated **border stretch** and the issue of **adverse possessions** (territories occupied by one country but legally belonging to another).
 
• **Ratification**: The **Constitution (100th Amendment) Bill** was passed by the **Rajya Sabha** on **May 6, 2015**, and by the **Lok Sabha** on **May 7, 2015**, reflecting a rare **political consensus** in the **Parliament of India**.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary objective to promote the 'Ultra Mega Power Projects' (UMPP) initiative in India?

options.text: Rooftop solar systems in rural areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High-capacity coal-based power plants**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary objective of the **Ultra Mega Power Projects (UMPP)** initiative is to develop **high-capacity coal-based power plants**, each having a capacity of approximately **4,000 MW** or more.
 
• These projects are designed to deliver power at **minimum cost** to consumers through **economies of scale** and the use of **supercritical technology**.
 
• The initiative was launched by the **Ministry of Power**, Government of India, in association with the **Power Finance Corporation (PFC)**, which acts as the nodal agency and **bid process coordinator**.
 
• The **UMPP** model involves **International Competitive Bidding (ICB)** to select developers who can build, own, and operate these massive energy infrastructures.
 
• Regarding the options provided in the question:
 
 
• **Rooftop solar systems in rural areas**: This refers to decentralized renewable energy initiatives like the **PM-KUSUM** or **Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Scheme**, not UMPP. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• **Small-scale solar plants**: These are typically handled under the **National Solar Mission** for localized energy needs. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• **Wind farms in rural areas**: Wind energy development is governed by the **National Offshore Wind Energy Policy** and other renewable targets, distinct from the coal-centric UMPP. **Hence, this statement is incorrect.**
 
• **High-capacity coal-based power plants**: This is the core definition and objective of the **Ultra Mega Power Projects** to ensure energy security for the **country**. **Hence, this statement is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Launch:** The **UMPP** scheme was initiated in **2005-06** to facilitate rapid capacity addition in the Indian power sector and to attract **private investment**.
 
• **Types of UMPPs:**
 
 
• **Pit-head projects:** Located near **coal mines**, where coal is transported via conveyor belts (e.g., **Sasan** in **Madhya Pradesh**).
 
• **Coastal projects:** Located at **coastal locations** to utilize **imported coal** arriving via sea routes (e.g., **Mundra** in **Gujarat**).
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Development:** For each project, a **Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)** is incorporated as a wholly-owned subsidiary of **PFC**. This SPV is responsible for obtaining **environmental clearances**, **land acquisition**, and **water allocation** before handing over the project to the successful bidder.
 
• **Key Examples:**
 
 
• **Mundra UMPP:** Located in **Gujarat**, developed by **Tata Power** (Coastal).
 
• **Sasan UMPP:** Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, developed by **Reliance Power** (Pit-head).
 
• **Krishnapatnam UMPP:** Located in **Andhra Pradesh** (Coastal).
 
• **Tilaiya UMPP:** Located in **Jharkhand** (Pit-head).
 
 
 
• **Features and Technology:** UMPPs utilize **supercritical technology**, which operates at higher **pressures and temperatures**, leading to **higher efficiency** and lower **carbon dioxide emissions** per unit of electricity generated compared to subcritical plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tariff-Based Bidding:** The developers are selected based on the **lowest levelized tariff** offered over a period of **25 years**, ensuring competitive pricing for state **distribution companies (DISCOMs)**.
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** These projects fall under the **Electricity Act, 2003**, and the **National Electricity Policy**, which aim to provide "Power for All" across the **Indian territory**.
 
• **Current Status:** While several UMPPs were planned, some faced delays due to issues in **coal block allocations**, **environmental concerns**, and changes in **international coal prices** (especially for coastal projects).
 
• **Data and Impact:** A single **4,000 MW** project can cater to the electricity needs of multiple **states**, significantly bridging the **peak demand-supply gap** in the **national grid**.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)?

options.text: To skill rural youth and promote wage employment opportunities
To supply subsidised agricultural inputs to farmers
To provide free food to rural households
To offer old-age pensions in villages

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To skill rural youth and promote wage employment opportunities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)** was launched on **25th September 2014** by the **Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD)**. The primary objective is to transform **rural poor youth** into an economically independent and globally relevant workforce.
 
• It is a **placement-linked skill training** program that targets **rural youth** between the **age** of **15 and 35 years**. For vulnerable groups like **women, persons with disabilities (PWDs), and SC/ST candidates**, the upper age limit is relaxed up to **45 years**.
 
• The scheme is a critical part of the **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM)**, focusing on adding diversity to the incomes of rural poor families and catering to the career aspirations of **rural youth**. *Hence, the statement regarding skilling rural youth for wage employment is correct.*
 
• DDU-GKY uniquely mandates that at least **70% of the trained candidates** must be guaranteed **placement** with a minimum salary of **₹6,000 per month** (or as per the minimum wages, whichever is higher). This ensures the scheme is outcome-oriented rather than just focusing on training.
 
• The scheme follows a **three-tier implementation model**, involving the **Ministry of Rural Development** at the national level, **State Rural Livelihood Missions (SRLM)** or State Skills Missions, and **Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs)** which are typically private or public sector training providers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of the Scheme**: DDU-GKY is the successor to the **Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana-Special Projects (SGSY-SP)**. It was revamped to focus specifically on **wage employment** in the formal sector rather than self-employment, which was the focus of earlier iterations.
 
• **Funding Pattern**: The funding for DDU-GKY is shared between the **Central Government** and the **State Governments** in a **60:40** ratio. However, for **North-Eastern States, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand**, the funding ratio is **90:10**.
 
• **Social Inclusion**: To ensure the benefits reach the most marginalized, the scheme mandates **earmarked coverage** for specific groups: **50%** for **SC/ST**, **15%** for **Minorities**, and **33%** for **Women**.
 
• **Geographical Coverage**: The scheme is implemented across **all states** and **Union Territories** of India. It specifically targets **rural areas** as defined by the **Census of India**.
 
• **International Standards**: The training provided under DDU-GKY is aligned with the **National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF)**, ensuring that the skills gained by the **rural youth** are recognized by employers across the **country** and even internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Champion Employers**: The program identifies "Champion Employers" who can provide **training and career progression** for at least **10,000 candidates** over a **2-year** period. This partnership helps in scaling up the impact of the **yojana**.
 
• **Alumni Support**: DDU-GKY provides post-placement support to candidates, such as **migration support centers**, to help **rural youth** adjust to urban work environments after their **placement**.
 
• **Global Outlook**: By **2020**, India was predicted to have a surplus of **55 million** working-age people, while the rest of the world faced a shortage. DDU-GKY aims to leverage this **demographic dividend** by preparing **youth** for global **employment** opportunities.

questions.question: In which of the following states did the Chhau dance originate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chhau dance** is a formidable semi-classical Indian dance with **martial, tribal, and folk traditions**, which found its primary origin in the **Seraikella** region of **Jharkhand**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Jharkhand is correct.***
 
• This dance form is deeply rooted in the local culture and is primarily performed by **male dancers** from families of traditional artists or from local communities.
 
• In **2010**, **UNESCO** inscribed **Chhau dance** on the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**, recognizing its cultural significance and unique artistic expression.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed during the **spring festival** known as **Chaitra Parva**, which typically falls in the **month of April** and lasts for thirteen days.
 
• It is characterized by its **vigorous movements**, **acrobatics**, and **athleticism**, which are derived from **martial arts** techniques (specifically **Parikhanda**) and **mock combat**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regional Variations:** There are three distinct styles of Chhau named after the locations where they are performed:

 
 
• **Seraikella Chhau**: Developed in the **Seraikella Kharsawan district** of **Jharkhand**. This style is known for its sophisticated use of **masks** to depict characters.
 
• **Purulia Chhau**: Developed in the **Purulia district** of **West Bengal**. This style also uses **masks**, which are typically larger and more theatrical than the Seraikella variety.
 
• **Mayurbhanj Chhau**: Developed in the **Mayurbhanj district** of **Odisha**. Unlike the other two, this style **does not use masks**, relying instead on facial expressions and body movements.
 
 
 
• **Themes and Narratives:** The dance performances usually depict episodes from great **Hindu epics** such as the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**, as well as stories from the **Puranas** and other Indian literature.
 
• **Musical Accompaniment:** The music is based on **folk melodies** and is played on traditional instruments such as the **Dhol** (a cylindrical drum), **Dhumsa** (a large kettle drum), and **Mohuri** (a reed instrument similar to the shehnai).
 
• **Costumes and Masks:** The **masks** are a central feature in the Jharkhand and West Bengal traditions, crafted by local artisans using **clay, paper-mâché, and cloth**. They are painted in vibrant colors to represent **gods, goddesses, demons, and animals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uttarakhand:** This state is famous for folk dances like **Chholiya**, which is a **martial art dance** performed during **marriages** and other celebrations. However, it is not the place of origin for Chhau. ***Hence, the statement regarding Uttarakhand is incorrect.***
 
• **Punjab:** The state of **Punjab** is world-renowned for the **Bhangra** and **Giddha** dance forms, which are energetic folk dances associated with the **harvest season** (Vaisakhi). These are distinct from the semi-classical nature of Chhau. ***Hence, the statement regarding Punjab is incorrect.***
 
• **Haryana:** Folk dances such as **Loor**, **Phag**, and **Dhamal** are native to **Haryana**. These dances are mostly related to **agriculture** and seasonal festivals like **Holi**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Haryana is incorrect.***
 
• **Cultural Impact:** **Chhau** serves as a powerful medium for **social cohesion**, bringing together people from different social strata and ethnic backgrounds to participate in the performance and the festivities of **Chaitra Parva**.
 
• **Modern Status:** Today, Chhau is recognized as one of the **classical-adjacent dances** of India, and the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** provides significant support for its preservation and promotion across **Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal**.
