questions.question: As per the 2025 Global Gender Gap Index, what rank did India secure among 148 countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**131**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Index** for the year **2025** (based on the latest comparative assessments of 148 nations) placed **India** at the **131st** rank, reflecting the nation's ongoing challenges and progress in achieving gender parity.
 
• The index is an annual publication released by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, an international non-governmental organization based in **Cologny, Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• The report evaluates countries across four critical dimensions: **Economic Participation and Opportunity**, **Educational Attainment**, **Health and Survival**, and **Political Empowerment**.
 
• In the **2025** assessment involving **148 countries**, India showed slight fluctuations compared to the previous years (such as **129th** in **2024**), highlighting specific gaps in **Economic Participation** and **Health** metrics.
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Index** scores range from **0 to 1**, where **1** represents full gender parity and **0** represents complete imparity; the **131st** rank indicates that India has a significant journey ahead to close the gender gap.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Origin**: The **Global Gender Gap Index** was first introduced by the **World Economic Forum** in **2006**. It was designed to measure gender-based gaps in access to resources and opportunities in countries rather than the actual level of the resources available.
 
• **Top Performers**: Historically, Nordic countries like **Iceland**, **Norway**, and **Finland** have consistently topped the index. **Iceland** has been the most gender-equal country in the world for over a decade, having closed more than **90%** of its gender gap.
 
• **The Four Pillars of Assessment**:
 
 
• **Economic Participation and Opportunity**: This includes indicators like **labour force participation rates**, **wage equality** for similar work, and the ratio of women in **senior-level positions**.
 
• **Educational Attainment**: This measures the gap between women’s and men’s access to **primary, secondary, and tertiary education** levels.
 
• **Health and Survival**: This pillar looks at the **sex ratio at birth** and **healthy life expectancy**.
 
• **Political Empowerment**: This measures the ratio of women in **parliament**, ministerial positions, and the number of years with a female **head of state**.
 
 
 
• **India's Context**: While India often performs relatively well in **Political Empowerment** due to historical leadership roles and local government reservations, it consistently lags in **Health and Survival** and **Economic Participation**, where the female **labour force participation rate (LFPR)** remains a point of concern.
 
• **Comparison with Other Indices**: The **Global Gender Gap Index** is distinct from the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, which is published by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**. The **GII** also considers reproductive health and **maternal mortality rates**, where India ranked **108th** in the **2022** report (released in **2024**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Data and Trends**: According to **WEF** reports, at the current rate of progress, it will take approximately **131 to 134 years** to reach full global gender parity.
 
• **Global Coverage**: The index has grown from **115 countries** in **2006** to **148 countries** in the **2025** cycle, making it one of the most comprehensive benchmarks for gender equality worldwide.
 
• **SDG 5**: The findings of this index are crucial for monitoring progress toward **Sustainable Development Goal 5 (SDG 5)**, which aims to achieve **gender equality** and empower all women and girls by the year **2030**.
 
• **Policy Influence**: Governments use this data to draft legislation, such as the **Women's Reservation Bill** (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam) passed in India in **September 2023**, which seeks to reserve **33%** of seats in the **Lok Sabha** and state assemblies for women.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts was enacted by the British Parliament to regulate the administration of the British East India Company’s territories in India, particularly in Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act, 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Regulating Act of 1773** was the first major step taken by the **British Parliament** to control and regulate the affairs of the **East India Company** in **India**. It recognized for the first time the political and administrative functions of the **Company**.
 
• This **Act** designated the **Governor of Bengal** as the **Governor-General of Bengal** and created an **Executive Council** of **four members** to assist him. **Lord Warren Hastings** was the first such **Governor-General**. ***Hence, the statement regarding regulation of Bengal's administration is correct.***
 
• It provided for the establishment of a **Supreme Court at Calcutta** in the year **1774**, comprising **one Chief Justice** and **three other judges**. **Sir Elijah Impey** was appointed as the first **Chief Justice**.
 
• The **Act** prohibited the servants of the **Company** from engaging in any **private trade** or accepting **presents and bribes** from the "natives," aiming to curb corruption within the administration.
 
• It strengthened the control of the **British Government** over the **Company** by requiring the **Court of Directors** (the governing body of the Company) to report on its **revenue, civil, and military affairs** in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pitt’s India Act, 1784**:

 
 
• This **Act** was passed to rectify the defects of the **Regulating Act of 1773**. It established a **system of double government** by creating a **Board of Control** to manage political affairs while the **Court of Directors** managed commercial affairs.
 
• For the first time, the **Company’s territories in India** were called the **“British possessions in India.”**
 
 
 
• **Charter Act, 1813**:
 
 
• This **Act** ended the **monopoly** of the **East India Company** over trade in **India**, except for trade in **tea** and trade with **China**.
 
• It allotted an annual sum of **one lakh rupees** for the **promotion of education** and knowledge of **sciences** among the inhabitants of **British India**.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1858**:

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025?

options.text: To allocate national funds for SDG projects
To monitor national-level progress of the 17 SDGs
To compare Indian SDGs with other countries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To monitor national-level progress of the 17 SDGs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary objective of the **Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report** is to provide a systematic and data-driven assessment of **India's progress** towards the **17 Sustainable Development Goals** and their associated **169 targets**.
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** serves as the nodal agency for developing and maintaining the **National Indicator Framework**, which was first circulated in **2018** and is refined annually.
 
• The report acts as a tracking tool to identify achievements, challenges, and gaps in **policy implementation** at the national level, ensuring that the development trajectory aligns with the **2030 Agenda**. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• While **resource mobilization** is important for **SDGs**, the specific purpose of the **NIF Progress Report** is monitoring and reporting, not the direct **allocation of national funds** for projects. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• The framework relies on existing **administrative data**, **national surveys**, and **census** information rather than conducting **primary environmental fieldwork** as its main function. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• Though international comparisons are conducted by the **United Nations** (e.g., Sustainable Development Report), the **National Indicator Framework** is specifically designed to reflect **national priorities** and internal progress within **India**. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** Also known as the **Global Goals**, they were adopted by the **United Nations** in **September 2015** as a universal call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity by the **year 2030**.
 
• **Structure of NIF:** The **National Indicator Framework** consists of nearly **280+ indicators** (the number varies with annual refinements) that translate the **global targets** into measurable units relevant to the **Indian socio-economic context**.
 
• **NITI Aayog's Role:** While **MoSPI** handles the **statistical framework** and data management, **NITI Aayog** is responsible for the overall **coordination and implementation** of **SDGs** in **India**, including the publication of the **SDG India Index**, which ranks **States and Union Territories**.
 
• **Key Themes:** The **17 SDGs** cover a wide range of issues, including **No Poverty (Goal 1)**, **Zero Hunger (Goal 2)**, **Quality Education (Goal 4)**, **Gender Equality (Goal 5)**, and **Climate Action (Goal 13)**.
 
• **Data Sources:** The progress report utilizes data from major sources such as the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**, **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)**, and various **Ministry-level administrative databases**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Institutional Mechanism:** India has established a **High-Level Steering Committee** chaired by the **Chief Statistician of India** to oversee the refinement of indicators within the **NIF**.
 
• **Evolution of Indicators:** The **NIF** is a dynamic document; for instance, in the **2024-2025** cycle, new indicators related to **digital economy** and **advanced healthcare** may be integrated to reflect modern **technological advancements**.
 
• **Global Reporting:** The data generated through the **NIF** also helps **India** in preparing its **Voluntary National Review (VNR)**, which is presented at the **United Nations High-Level Political Forum (HLPF)**.
 
• **Localization of SDGs:** Beyond the national level, the **NIF** encourages the creation of **State Indicator Frameworks (SIF)** and **District Indicator Frameworks (DIF)** to ensure progress reaches the grassroots level across the **700+ districts** of **India**.

questions.question: Which among the following statements is INCORRECT related to the Right to Information Act, 2005?

options.text: It covers all constitutional authorities, including the President and the Supreme Court.
All the non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that are financed by the government come under the purview of RTI Act.
The Act mandates that the information be provided within 30 days of the request in normal cases.
The Central Information Commission is a constitutional body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Central Information Commission is a constitutional body.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005** defines "Public Authority" under **Section 2(h)**, which includes any body or institution of self-government established or constituted by or under the **Constitution**. This ensures it covers all constitutional authorities, including the **President**, the **Supreme Court**, and the **High Courts**. Hence, the statement "It covers all constitutional authorities, including the President and the Supreme Court" is **correct**.
 
• The scope of the **RTI Act** extends to **Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)** that are substantially financed, directly or indirectly, by funds provided by the appropriate **Government**. This is mandated to ensure transparency in organizations utilizing public money. Hence, the statement "All the non-governmental organizations (NGOs) that are financed by the government come under the purview of RTI Act" is **correct**.
 
• According to **Section 7(1)** of the Act, a **Public Information Officer (PIO)** is required to provide the requested information within **30 days** of the receipt of the request in normal circumstances. If the information sought concerns the **life or liberty** of a person, it must be provided within **48 hours**. Hence, the statement "The Act mandates that the information be provided within 30 days of the request in normal cases" is **correct**.
 
• The **Central Information Commission (CIC)** was established under the provisions of the **Right to Information Act, 2005**. Since it was created by an **Act of Parliament** and not mentioned in the original text of the **Constitution of India**, it is a **statutory body**, not a constitutional body. Hence, the statement "The Central Information Commission is a constitutional body" is **incorrect**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Right to Information Act** was enacted in **June 2005** and came into full force on **12 October 2005**. It replaced the erstwhile **Freedom of Information Act, 2002** to provide a more robust framework for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities.
 
• The **Central Information Commission (CIC)** consists of the **Chief Information Commissioner** and not more than **ten Central Information Commissioners**. They are appointed by the **President of India** on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the **Prime Minister** (as Chairperson), the **Leader of Opposition** in the Lok Sabha, and a **Union Cabinet Minister** nominated by the Prime Minister.
 
• The primary objective of the **RTI Act** is to empower citizens, promote **transparency** and **accountability** in the working of the Government, contain **corruption**, and make our democracy work for the people in a real sense. It applies to both the **Central** and **State Governments** (except for certain intelligence and security organizations).
 
• In **2019**, the **RTI (Amendment) Act** was passed, which changed the **tenure** and **salary** structures of the Information Commissioners. Under the **2019 amendment**, the **Central Government** now notifies the term of office and determines the salaries and allowances, which were previously fixed by the original **2005 Act**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Exemptions from Disclosure**: Under **Section 8** of the RTI Act, certain categories of information are exempt from disclosure, such as information that would prejudicially affect the **sovereignty and integrity** of India, **security**, strategic, scientific or economic interests of the State, or relation with **foreign States**.
 
• **First Appeal**: If a citizen does not receive a decision within the specified **30 days** or is aggrieved by the decision of the **PIO**, they can file a **First Appeal** under **Section 19(1)** to an officer senior in rank to the PIO within **30 days**.
 
• **Second Appeal**: A **Second Appeal** can be filed under **Section 19(3)** against the decision of the First Appellate Authority before the **Central Information Commission** or the **State Information Commission** within **90 days**.
 
• **Penalties**: The Commission can impose a penalty of **Rs. 250 per day** (up to a maximum of **Rs. 25,000**) on a PIO who has failed to accept an application or delayed providing information without reasonable cause.

questions.question: The average marks of 17 students in a class is 40. If the marks of each student are doubled, find the new average.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Property: If each observation in a data set is multiplied by a constant 'k', the average is also multiplied by 'k'.

Here, Old Average = 40 and marks are doubled (k = 2).

New Average = Old Average × 2

New Average = 40 × 2 = 80

**∴ Answer = 80**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Number of students = 17

Average marks of 17 students = 40

Condition: Marks of each student are doubled.

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Number of observations

Sum = Average × Number of observations

 Initial Avg: 40 
 
 Doubled (×2) New Avg: 80 Number of Students = 17 (Constant) 

**Calculations:**

Initial total marks of 17 students = 17 × 40 = 680

⇒ If marks of each student are doubled, the new total marks = 680 × 2

⇒ New total marks = 1360

⇒ New Average = New total marks ÷ Number of students

⇒ New Average = 1360 ÷ 17

⇒ New Average = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80 (Option 3).**

Addition/Subtraction Property

If a constant 'k' is added to or subtracted from each observation, the new average becomes (Old Average + k) or (Old Average − k).

Division Property

If each observation is divided by a non-zero constant 'k', the new average becomes (Old Average ÷ k).

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, Weighted Avg = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: The primary "food" or energy source produced by the plant during photosynthesis is a type of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbohydrate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Photosynthesis** is the biological process by which **green plants**, algae, and certain bacteria convert **light energy** into **chemical energy**. This process is the primary way that energy enters the **biosphere**.
 
• The main "food" produced during this process is **Glucose**, which is a type of **Carbohydrate**. Specifically, it is a **monosaccharide** or simple sugar with the chemical formula **C6H12O6**.
 
• During photosynthesis, plants take in **Carbon dioxide (CO2)** from the air and **Water (H2O)** from the soil. Using the energy from **sunlight**, they transform these inorganic molecules into **organic energy-rich carbohydrates**.
 
• The process takes place primarily in the **leaves** of the plant, within specialized cellular structures called **chloroplasts**. These organelles contain **chlorophyll**, the **green pigment** responsible for absorbing light.
 
• The **chemical equation** representing this reaction is: **6CO2 + 6H2O + Light Energy → C6H12O6 + 6O2**. This shows that for every molecule of **glucose** produced, six molecules of **oxygen** are released into the atmosphere as a **byproduct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Carbohydrates in Plants:**

 
 
• **Glucose**: The immediate product of photosynthesis used for **cellular respiration** to provide **ATP (energy)** for the plant.
 
• **Starch**: Since glucose is soluble in water, plants convert excess glucose into **starch** (a complex carbohydrate) for **long-term energy storage** in roots, tubers, and seeds.
 
• **Cellulose**: Another complex carbohydrate produced from glucose that forms the **structural component** of the **plant cell wall**, providing **rigidity** and strength.
 
 
 
• **Other Biomolecules (Incorrect Options):**
 
 
• **Proteins**: While plants do synthesize proteins, they are not the primary product of photosynthesis. Proteins are made from **amino acids**, which require **nitrogen** absorbed from the soil in the form of **nitrates**.
 
• **Minerals**: These are **inorganic elements** like **Magnesium**, **Potassium**, and **Phosphorus** that plants absorb from the soil; they are not "produced" by the plant but are essential for **enzymatic functions**.
 
• **Vitamins**: Plants synthesize various **vitamins** (like Vitamin C and A) as **organic micronutrients** for their own metabolic processes, but these are not the primary energy source.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Chlorophyll:**
 
 
• **Chlorophyll a and b** are the most common types of pigments found in **terrestrial plants**. They absorb light most efficiently in the **blue** and **red** wavelengths of the **visible spectrum**, while reflecting **green** light.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Factors:**
 
 
• The **rate of photosynthesis** is influenced by several factors including **light intensity**, **carbon dioxide concentration**, and **temperature** (optimum usually between **25°C to 35°C**).
 
• The discovery of the **Calvin Cycle** (the dark reaction) in the **mid-20th century** by **Melvin Calvin** explained how plants turn CO2 into **carbohydrates**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Autotrophs**: Plants are known as **photoautotrophs** because they manufacture their own food using light. They form the **first trophic level** in almost every **food chain**.
 
• **Oxygen Cycle**: Photosynthesis is crucial for maintaining **atmospheric oxygen** levels. It is estimated that **marine plants (phytoplankton)** produce between **50% to 80%** of the Earth's oxygen.
 
• **Carbon Sequestration**: By absorbing **CO2**, plants play a vital role in **mitigating climate change** and the **greenhouse effect**.
 
• **Phloem Transport**: Once produced, the carbohydrates (usually in the form of **sucrose**) are transported from the leaves to other parts of the plant through the **vascular tissue** called **phloem**.

• The **Taskbar** houses the **Notification Area** (also known as the **System Tray**), which displays **system settings** such as the **date and time**, **battery status**, **network connectivity**, and **volume control**.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with the Official Languages of the Indian Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XVII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XVII** of the **Constitution of India** contains the provisions relating to the **Official Languages** of the Union and the states.
 
• It encompasses **Articles 343 to 351** and is divided into four distinct chapters covering the **Language of the Union**, **Regional Languages**, **Language of the Supreme Court and High Courts**, and **Special Directives**.
 
• **Article 343** explicitly states that the **Official Language** of the **Union** shall be **Hindi** in **Devanagari script**, while the form of numerals to be used for official purposes shall be the international form of **Indian numerals**.
 
• The **Constitution** originally provided for the use of the **English language** for all official purposes of the Union for a period of **15 years** from the date of its commencement (i.e., until **January 25, 1965**).
 
• Under **Article 344**, the **President of India** is mandated to constitute a **Commission** at the expiration of **five years** from the commencement of the Constitution, and thereafter at the expiration of **ten years**, to make recommendations regarding the progressive use of **Hindi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part XV**:

 
 
• This part deals with **Elections** and contains **Articles 324 to 329A**.
 
• It provides for the establishment of the **Election Commission of India**, which is responsible for the direction and control of **Parliamentary** and **State Legislature elections**.
 
• It also mentions the principle of **Adult Suffrage**, ensuring every citizen above the **age of 18** has the right to vote.
 
 
 
• **Part XVI**:
 
 
• This part consists of **Special Provisions Relating to Certain Classes**, covering **Articles 330 to 342**.
 
• It includes reservations for **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** in the **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies**.
 
• It also defines the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes**.
 
 
 
• **Part XX**:
 
 
• This part contains a single **Article 368**, which grants **Parliament** the power to **amend the Constitution**.
 
• It outlines the procedure for amendments, which may require a **simple majority**, **special majority**, or **special majority with ratification by half of the states**, depending on the nature of the provision.
 
 
 
• **Official Languages Act, 1963**:
 
 
• Since **Hindi** could not completely replace **English** by **1965**, this **Act** was passed to provide for the continued use of **English** for official purposes of the **Union** and for use in **Parliament** indefinitely.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eighth Schedule**: This schedule of the **Indian Constitution** lists the **22 official languages** recognized by the state. Initially, there were **14 languages**, but others were added through various **Constitutional Amendment Acts** (e.g., **21st**, **71st**, and **92nd Amendments**).
 
• **Classical Languages**: Apart from official languages, the **Government of India** grants the status of **Classical Language** to those with high antiquity. Currently, **six languages** hold this status: **Tamil (2004)**, **Sanskrit (2005)**, **Kannada (2008)**, **Telugu (2008)**, **Malayalam (2013)**, and **Odia (2014)**.
 
• **Article 351**: This article contains a **Special Directive** for the development of the **Hindi language**, directing the **Union** to promote the spread of **Hindi** so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all elements of the **composite culture** of **India**.
 
• **Article 348**: It specifies that until **Parliament** provides otherwise, all proceedings in the **Supreme Court** and every **High Court**, as well as the authoritative texts of all **Bills**, **Acts**, and **Ordinances**, shall be in the **English language**.

questions.question: Stand Up India Scheme was launched in which of the following years?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Stand Up India Scheme** was officially launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **5th April 2016**. The launch event took place in **Noida, Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The primary objective of this scheme is to promote **entrepreneurship** at the grassroots level, specifically focusing on **economic empowerment** and **job creation** among **Scheduled Castes (SC)**, **Scheduled Tribes (ST)**, and **Women** entrepreneurs.
 
• The scheme facilitates **bank loans** between **Rs. 10 lakh and Rs. 1 crore** to at least one **SC** or **ST** borrower and at least one **woman** borrower per bank branch of all **Scheduled Commercial Banks**.
 
• It is specifically designed for setting up **Greenfield enterprises**, which refers to the first-time venture of the beneficiary in the **manufacturing**, **services**, **agri-allied activities**, or **trading sector**.
 
• The **Department of Financial Services (DFS)**, under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency governing the implementation of this scheme across the **country**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligibility and Ownership:** To benefit from the scheme, the entrepreneur must be above **18 years of age**. In the case of non-individual enterprises, at least **51%** of the shareholding and controlling stake must be held by either an **SC/ST** or **Woman entrepreneur**.
 
• **Loan Repayment and Moratorium:** The loan provided under the scheme is repayable in **7 years**, and the maximum permissible **moratorium period** is **18 months**.
 
• **Margin Money:** Initially, the scheme required the borrower to provide **25%** margin money. However, to make the scheme more accessible, the **Government of India** later reduced the margin money requirement to **15%** of the project cost.
 
• **Support Ecosystem:** The scheme is supported by the **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** and the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)**. The **Stand Up Mitra portal** was created to provide a digital interface for applicants to access loans and handholding support.
 
• **Extension of the Scheme:** Recognizing its impact on financial inclusion, the **Union Budget** has extended the **Stand Up India Scheme** up to the **year 2025** to continue fostering an entrepreneurial culture among underserved sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Context of Other Years:**

 
 
• In **2014**, the government launched the **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** on **28th August**, which is the **world's largest financial inclusion** initiative.
 
• In **2015**, several major schemes were introduced, including the **Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY)** on **8th April** and the **Digital India** campaign on **1st July**.
 
• In **2019**, the **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)** was launched to provide income support to all landholding farmers' families in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Credit Guarantee:** To encourage banks to lend, the government created the **Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI)**, which provides a guarantee for the loans granted under the scheme, thereby reducing the **risk factor** for financial institutions.
 
• **Impact Data:** Since its inception in **2016**, the scheme has sanctioned over **Rs. 40,000 crore** to more than **1.8 lakh** accounts, significantly boosting **women empowerment** and financial independence in **rural and urban India**.

questions.question: Which action connected with the new rifle system offended the religious beliefs of Indian sepoys and became a major cause of discontent in 1857?

options.text: Imposing a ban on temple entry
Mandating Sunday church attendance for all soldiers
Prohibiting religious processions in army cantonments
Forcing sepoys to bite cartridges greased with animal fat

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Forcing sepoys to bite cartridges greased with animal fat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The immediate cause of the **Revolt of 1857** was the introduction of the **Enfield P-53 Rifle** in the **British East India Company's** army. The cartridges for this new rifle were rumored to be greased with **animal fat**, specifically from **cows and pigs**.
 
• To load the rifle, soldiers (sepoys) were required to **bite off the top of the cartridge** before inserting it into the muzzle. This action directly violated the religious tenets of both **Hindu and Muslim** soldiers.
 
• For **Hindus**, the **cow** is considered a sacred animal, and consuming or touching its fat was seen as a grave sin and a loss of caste. For **Muslims**, the **pig** is considered **Haram** (forbidden), and contact with its fat was religiously offensive.
 
• This perceived attempt at **forced conversion** or defilement of their faith led to widespread suspicion that the **British** were trying to destroy the traditional religions of India to facilitate the spread of **Christianity**.
 
• The first major act of defiance occurred on **March 29, 1857**, at **Barrackpore**, where **Mangal Pandey** of the **34th Native Infantry** attacked his British officers, refusing to use the greased cartridges. This event served as a catalyst for the larger rebellion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Political Causes:** The aggressive expansion policies of **Lord Dalhousie**, particularly the **Doctrine of Lapse**, caused resentment among Indian royalty. States like **Satara (1848)**, **Jhansi (1853)**, and **Nagpur (1854)** were annexed when their rulers died without a natural male heir. The annexation of **Awadh** in **1856** on grounds of "maladministration" further angered the sepoys, many of whom hailed from that region.
 
• **Military Grievances:** Indian sepoys faced systemic discrimination, including **lower pay** compared to British soldiers and limited opportunities for promotion. The **General Service Enlistment Act of 1856**, passed by **Lord Canning**, required sepoys to serve **overseas** if needed, which crossed the "black waters" (**Kala Pani**) and was believed to cause a loss of caste for Hindus.
 
• **Social and Religious Reforms:** British initiatives like the **Abolition of Sati (1829)**, the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (1856)**, and the promotion of **Western education** were viewed by conservative sections of society as an interference in Indian social customs and religious life.
 
• **Economic Exploitation:** The high **land revenue** demands under the **Ryotwari** and **Mahalwari** systems, coupled with the destruction of traditional Indian **handicrafts** due to the influx of British manufactured goods, led to widespread poverty and rural indebtedness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timeline of the Revolt:** While the Barrackpore incident happened in March, the formal outbreak of the revolt began on **May 10, 1857**, in **Meerut**. The rebellious soldiers marched to **Delhi** and proclaimed the aging Mughal Emperor, **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, as the **Emperor of Hindustan**.
 
• **Key Centers and Leaders:**
 
 
• **Delhi:** Led by **General Bakht Khan** (nominal head Bahadur Shah Zafar).
 
• **Kanpur:** Led by **Nana Saheb** (the adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II) and **Tantia Tope**.
 
• **Lucknow:** Led by **Begum Hazrat Mahal**.
 
• **Jhansi:** Led by **Rani Lakshmibai**, who fought valiantly against **Sir Hugh Rose**.
 
• **Bihar (Arrah):** Led by the elderly zamindar **Kunwar Singh**.
 
 
 
• **Consequences:** The revolt led to the end of the **East India Company's** rule. Under the **Government of India Act 1858**, the administration of India was transferred directly to the **British Crown**. **Lord Canning** became the first **Viceroy** of India, and the office of the **Secretary of State for India** was created.

questions.question: ₹6320 is divided among A, B, C, and D in such a way that the shares of A and B, B and C, and C and D are in the ratios of 2 : 3, 4 : 5, and 10 : 3 respectively. The share of A (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A:B = 2:3, B:C = 4:5 ⇒ make B same (LCM=12)

⇒ A:B = 8:12, B:C = 12:15 ⇒ A:B:C = 8:12:15

⇒ C:D = 10:3 ⇒ make C=30 ⇒ multiply by 2

⇒ A:B:C:D = 16:24:30:9

⇒ Total = 79 parts

⇒ A = (16/79)×6320 = 1280

**∴ Answer = 1280**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A : B = 2 : 3

B : C = 4 : 5

C : D = 10 : 3

**Concept Used:**

Chain ratio method

**Calculation:**

⇒ A : B = 2 : 3

⇒ B : C = 4 : 5

⇒ Make B equal (LCM of 3 and 4 = 12)

⇒ A : B = 8 : 12

⇒ B : C = 12 : 15

⇒ So A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15

⇒ C : D = 10 : 3

⇒ Make C equal (LCM of 15 and 10 = 30)

⇒ A : B : C = 16 : 24 : 30

⇒ C : D = 30 : 9

⇒ Final ratio A : B : C : D = 16 : 24 : 30 : 9

⇒ Total parts = 16 + 24 + 30 + 9 = 79

⇒ Share of A = (16 ÷ 79) × 6320

⇒ = 1280

**∴ Share of A = 1280**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Chain Ratio:** Equalize common terms stepwise

**LCM Trick:** Use LCM to match ratios

**Division Rule:** Share = (Part ÷ Total) × Amount

**Shortcut Tip:** Combine ratios before calculating share

questions.question: Which type of receptors in the human body are responsible for detecting taste?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gustatory receptors**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gustatory receptors** are the specialized **sensory receptors** responsible for detecting **taste**. They are primarily located on the **tongue** within structures known as **taste buds**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Gustatory receptors is correct.***
 
• These receptors function by reacting to **chemical stimuli** dissolved in **saliva**. When we eat, the molecules in food bind to these receptors, sending **neural impulses** to the **brain** to interpret flavors.
 
• **Auditory receptors**, also known as **hair cells**, are located in the **inner ear** (specifically the **cochlea**). Their primary **function** is to detect **sound vibrations** and convert them into **electrical signals** for the **auditory nerve**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Auditory receptors is incorrect.***
 
• **Thermo receptors** are **sensory nerve endings** that respond to changes in **temperature**. They are widely distributed throughout the **skin** and **mucous membranes** to help the body maintain **homeostasis**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Thermo receptors is incorrect.***
 
• **Olfactory receptors** are located in the **upper part** of the **nasal cavity**. They are responsible for the sense of **smell** by detecting **volatile chemical substances** in the air. ***Hence, the statement regarding Olfactory receptors is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Sense of Taste (Gustation)**:

 
 
• The **location** of taste receptors is not limited to the tongue; they are also found on the **soft palate**, **upper esophagus**, **cheek**, and **epiglottis**.
 
• Humans typically have between **2,000 and 10,000** taste buds. Each taste bud contains **50 to 100** gustatory receptor cells.
 
• The **functions** of these receptors include helping the **organism** identify **nutrients** and avoid **toxic substances**, which often have a **bitter** taste.
 
 
 
• **The Five Basic Tastes**:
 
 
• **Sweet**: Usually triggered by **carbohydrates** like **glucose** and **fructose**.
 
• **Sour**: Detected when **hydrogen ions** from **acids** (like **citric acid** in lemons) enter the receptor cells.
 
• **Salty**: Primarily produced by **sodium chloride** (**table salt**).
 
• **Bitter**: Often a warning sign, as many **poisonous plants** contain **alkaloids** that taste bitter.
 
• **Umami**: A **savory** taste associated with **glutamate**, commonly found in **meat**, **cheese**, and **soy sauce**.
 
 
 
• **Interconnected Senses**:
 
 
• The sense of **taste** is closely linked to the sense of **smell**. Approximately **80%** of what we perceive as **flavor** is actually derived from **olfactory stimuli**. This is why food often tastes bland when a person has a **blocked nose** due to a **cold**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Age and Perception**: The number of functional **gustatory receptors** decreases with **age**. Most people start to lose some of their taste buds around the **age of 50**, which can lead to a reduced **appetite** in **elderly** individuals.
 
• **Neural Pathways**: Information from the **taste buds** is carried to the **brain** via three **cranial nerves**: the **Facial nerve (VII)**, the **Glossopharyngeal nerve (IX)**, and the **Vagus nerve (X)**. These signals reach the **gustatory cortex** in the **parietal lobe** of the **brain**.
 
• **Photoreceptors**: Another key type of receptor in the **human body** is the **photoreceptor** (**rods and cones**), located in the **retina** of the **eye**, which are responsible for **vision**.
 
• **Clinical Significance**: A complete loss of the sense of taste is called **ageusia**, while a reduced ability to taste is known as **hypogeusia**. These conditions can be caused by **deficiencies** (like **Zinc**), **medications**, or **neurological disorders**.

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

17, 67

22, 87
questions.solution:

**17 → 67**

⇒ 17 × 4 = 68

⇒ 68 − 1 = 67

**22 → 87**

⇒ 22 × 4 = 88

⇒ 88 − 1 = 87

Now, applying the same logic to the options:

⇒ 24 × 4 = 96

⇒ 96 + 3 = 99

⇒ 100 − 2 = 98 

Option 4) 24, 98

⇒ 96 + 2 = 98 

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question: A man can row 8 km/hr in still water while speed of current is 3 km/hr. How much time (in hours) will he take to row 11 km downstream and 15 km upstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Downstream speed = 8 + 3 = 11 km/hr

⇒ Upstream speed = 8 − 3 = 5 km/hr

⇒ Time = (11/11) + (15/5)

⇒ = 1 + 3 = 4 hr

**∴ Answer = 4 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed in still water = 8 km/hr

Speed of current = 3 km/hr

Distance downstream = 11 km

Distance upstream = 15 km

**Concept Used:**

Downstream speed = u + v

Upstream speed = u − v

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Downstream speed = 8 + 3 = 11 km/hr

⇒ Time downstream = 11 ÷ 11 = 1 hr

⇒ Upstream speed = 8 − 3 = 5 km/hr

⇒ Time upstream = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 hr

questions.question: According to the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2025, which pollutant was identified as the primary cause of increased respiratory illnesses due to air pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particulate matter (PM2.5)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Particulate Matter (PM2.5)** consists of fine inhalable particles with diameters that are generally **2.5 micrometers** and smaller. These are significant because they are small enough to penetrate deep into the **gas-exchange regions** of the lungs and enter the **bloodstream**.
 
• According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)** in **2025**, **PM2.5** continues to be the most dangerous pollutant for human health, responsible for millions of premature deaths globally due to **respiratory infections**, **lung cancer**, and **cardiovascular diseases**.
 
• The **WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines** provide clear evidence of the damage air pollution inflicts on human health, at even lower concentrations than previously understood, particularly highlighting the **morbidity** associated with fine particulate matter.
 
• These particles originate from various sources, including **power plants**, **industrial processes**, **vehicle exhausts**, and **biomass burning**. Because they remain suspended in the air for long periods and can travel great distances, they pose a transboundary health risk.
 
• Clinical studies associated with the **2025 report** indicate that long-term exposure to **PM2.5** is a primary driver for the increased incidence of **Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)** and **Asthma** exacerbations across urban populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ozone (O₃)**: Unlike the protective layer in the stratosphere, **Ground-level Ozone** is a harmful air pollutant. It is not emitted directly but is created by **chemical reactions** between oxides of nitrogen (**NOx**) and volatile organic compounds (**VOCs**) in the presence of **sunlight**. It is a major component of **smog** and triggers chest pain, coughing, and throat irritation.
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**: A **colorless, odorless gas** that is produced by the incomplete combustion of **carbon-based fuels**. When inhaled, it binds to **hemoglobin** in the blood more effectively than oxygen, reducing the amount of oxygen reaching the body's organs and tissues, which can be fatal in high concentrations.
 
• **Sulphur Dioxide (SO₂)**: Primarily produced from the burning of **fossil fuels** (coal and oil) and the smelting of **mineral ores**. It contributes to the formation of **acid rain** and can cause **bronchoconstriction** and increased **asthma** symptoms.
 
• **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)**: This gas is part of a group of highly reactive gases known as **oxides of nitrogen**. It is primarily expelled from **motor vehicle engines** and **power plants**. High concentrations can inflame the **airways** and reduce **lung function**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI)**: This is a **numerical scale** used by government agencies to communicate to the public how polluted the air currently is or how polluted it is forecast to become. As the **AQI** increases, an increasingly large percentage of the population is likely to experience severe adverse health effects.
 
• **WHO Guidelines (2021/2025 Update)**: The recommended annual mean level for **PM2.5** is **5 µg/m³**. This target is set to minimize health risks, though many **developing countries** and industrial hubs frequently record values exceeding **50 µg/m³**.
 
• **Vulnerable Groups**: The impact of air pollution is not uniform; **children**, the **elderly**, and people with **pre-existing heart or lung conditions** are at a significantly higher risk of complications from **PM2.5** exposure.
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**: In the context of **India**, this initiative aims to achieve a **20% to 30% reduction** in particulate matter concentrations by **2024-2026** compared to **2017** levels, focusing on **non-attainment cities**.

questions.question: Which of the following languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**English**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eighth Schedule** to the **Constitution of India** lists the official languages of the Republic of India. Currently, it consists of **22 languages**.
 
• **Sanskrit** is one of the original **14 languages** that were included in the **Eighth Schedule** at the commencement of the Constitution in **1950**. **Sanskrit** is also recognized as a **Classical Language** of India. ***Hence, the statement regarding Sanskrit being included is correct.***
 
• **Urdu** was also among the original **14 languages** included in the **Eighth Schedule** in **1950**. It is widely spoken across various parts of **India**, particularly in states like **Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Urdu being included is correct.***
 
• **Nepali** was added to the **Eighth Schedule** by the **71st Amendment Act** in the year **1992**, along with **Konkani and Manipuri**. It is primarily spoken in the state of **Sikkim** and the **Darjeeling** district of **West Bengal**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Nepali being included is correct.***
 
• **English** is **NOT** included in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution**. While **English** is an **official language** for the transaction of business in the **Parliament** and for communication between the **Union and States** under **Article 343**, it does not have a place in the list of 22 scheduled languages. ***Hence, the statement regarding English NOT being included is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of the Eighth Schedule:**

 
 
• Initially, there were only **14 languages**: **Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu**.
 
• The **21st Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1967** added **Sindhi** as the 15th language.
 
• The **71st Constitutional Amendment Act** of **1992** added **Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali**.
 
• The **92nd Constitutional Amendment Act** of **2003** (which came into force in **2004**) added four more languages: **Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali**, bringing the total count to **22**.
 
 
 
• **Official Language vs. Scheduled Language:**
 
 
• **Article 343** declares **Hindi** in **Devanagari script** as the **Official Language** of the **Union**. **English** was permitted to be used for official purposes for a period of **15 years**, but the **Official Languages Act, 1963**, allowed for its continued use indefinitely.
 
• While **English** is the **official language** of states like **Nagaland and Mizoram**, it remains absent from the **Eighth Schedule**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Inclusion:**
 
 
• Languages in this schedule are represented on the **Official Languages Commission**. Candidates appearing for **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** examinations can opt to take the exam in any of these **22 languages**.
 
• The **Government of India** is under an obligation to take measures for the development of these languages.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Classical Languages:** Apart from the **Eighth Schedule**, the **Government of India** grants the status of **"Classical Language"** to certain languages that have a high antiquity of early texts and a recorded history over a period of **1500-2000 years**. Currently, these include **Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Kannada (2008), Telugu (2008), Malayalam (2013), and Odia (2014)**.
 
• **Demands for Inclusion:** There are persistent demands to include more languages like **Tulu, Rajasthani, and Bhojpuri** in the **Eighth Schedule**. Decisions on these are usually based on the recommendations of committees like the **Pahwa Committee (1996)** and the **Sitakant Mohapatra Committee (2003)**.
 
• **Article 351:** This article provides a **Directive** for the development of the **Hindi language**, stating that it should draw its vocabulary primarily from **Sanskrit** and secondarily from other languages mentioned in the **Eighth Schedule**.

questions.question: The Trans-Siberian Railways major rail route of Russia runs from St. Petersburg in the west to _______ on the Pacific Coast in the east.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vladivostok**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Trans-Siberian Railway** is the longest railway system in the world, stretching across the vast expanse of **Russia**. It is a massive network that connects **European Russia** with the **Russian Far East**.
 
• The major route of this railway begins at **St. Petersburg** in the west, passes through **Moscow**, and reaches its eastern terminus at **Vladivostok** on the **Pacific Coast**.
 
• The construction of this monumental project began in **1891** under the reign of **Tsar Alexander III** and was completed in **1916**. It covers a total distance of approximately **9,289 kilometers** (5,772 miles).
 
• The railway was designed to serve several functions, including **military transport**, **administrative control** of distant territories, and the **economic development** of the **Siberian region**.
 
• It crosses **eight time zones** and passes through various geographic features, including the **Ural Mountains**, the **Siberian taiga**, and runs along the shores of **Lake Baikal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Novosibirsk:** This city is a major stop on the Trans-Siberian route. Founded in **1893** specifically as a crossing point for the railway over the **Ob River**, it has grown into the third-largest city in **Russia** and is known as the "Capital of Siberia."
 
• **Moscow:** While the route historically starts in **St. Petersburg**, **Moscow** serves as the primary hub where many travelers begin their journey. It acts as the central junction connecting the **Trans-Siberian** with other **European rail networks**.
 
• **Irkutsk:** Located near the southern tip of **Lake Baikal**, **Irkutsk** is often called the "Paris of Siberia" due to its historic architecture. It is a critical cultural and economic center in **Eastern Siberia** along the rail line.
 
• **Branches of the Railway:** Besides the main line to **Vladivostok**, the network includes the **Trans-Manchurian** line and the **Trans-Mongolian** line, which provide rail links to **Beijing**, **China**, and **Ulaanbaatar**, **Mongolia**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The railway allows for the large-scale export of **natural resources** such as **timber**, **coal**, and **minerals** from **Siberia** to both **European** and **Asian markets**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vladivostok:** The name of the city literally means "Ruler of the East." It is a vital **deep-water port** on the **Sea of Japan** and serves as the home base for the **Russian Navy's Pacific Fleet**.
 
• **Technical Feats:** The railway is fully **electrified** since **2002**, allowing for more efficient transport of heavy freight. It involves crossing massive rivers like the **Volga**, **Irtysh**, **Ob**, **Yenisei**, and **Amur** via lengthy railway bridges.
 
• **Global Logistics:** In the modern era, the Trans-Siberian is a key component of the **"New Silk Road"** or the **Eurasian Land Bridge**, facilitating **container traffic** between **East Asia** and **Europe** as an alternative to sea routes through the **Suez Canal**.
 
• **Tourism:** The route is a world-famous tourist attraction, with the journey from **Moscow** to **Vladivostok** typically taking about **six to seven days** of continuous travel.

In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Q. Five people – Riya, Meena, Tanu, Sunita, and Kavita – are sitting in a row facing north.

Who is sitting exactly in the middle of the row?

(I) Tanu sits immediately to the right of Meena, and Sunita sits immediately to the right of Tanu.

(II) Riya is at one of the ends, and Kavita sits immediately to the left of Riya.

options.text: Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement II is not
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in Statement I is not

questions.solution:
Given:

Five people – Riya, Meena, Tanu, Sunita, and Kavita – are sitting in a row facing north.

We need to find who is sitting exactly in the middle (3rd position).

Now,

Statement (I):

Tanu sits immediately to the right of Meena, and Sunita sits immediately to the right of Tanu.

⇒ Meena – Tanu – Sunita form a block of three consecutive seats

⇒ But Riya and Kavita positions are not fixed

⇒ Middle position cannot be uniquely identified

⇒ Statement I alone is not sufficient

Statement (II):

Riya is at one of the ends, and Kavita sits immediately to the left of Riya

⇒ If Riya is at an end, Kavita cannot be immediately left of Riya (since left side is undefined at extreme left or right depending on position ambiguity)

⇒ Even if interpreted, remaining people positions are still not fixed uniquely

⇒ Statement II alone is not sufficient

Now, combining (I) and (II):

From (I): Meena – Tanu – Sunita are consecutive

From (II): Riya is at an end and Kavita is next to her

Now, possible arrangement becomes fixed as:

Riya – Kavita – Meena – Tanu – Sunita

So, middle position (3rd) is Meena

Thus, both statements together are sufficient.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India authorises Parliament to alter the applicability of Fundamental Rights with respect to members of the Armed Forces and the forces entrusted with the maintenance of public order?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 33**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 33** of the **Constitution of India** empowers the **Parliament** to restrict or abrogate the **Fundamental Rights** of the members of the **Armed Forces**, **paramilitary forces**, **police forces**, **intelligence agencies**, and analogous forces.
 
• The primary objective of **Article 33** is to ensure the **proper discharge of their duties** and the **maintenance of discipline** among them, which is vital for national security and public order.
 
• This power to make laws under **Article 33** is conferred exclusively on the **Parliament** and not on the **State Legislatures**.
 
• Any law made by **Parliament** under this article cannot be challenged in any court on the ground of contravention of any of the **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed by **Part III** of the **Constitution**.
 
• The scope of "members of the armed forces" under **Article 33** also covers non-combatant employees such as **barbers**, **carpenters**, **mechanics**, **cooks**, **tailors**, and others who are part of the establishment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 35:**

 
 
• It provides that the power to make laws, to give effect to certain specified **Fundamental Rights**, shall vest only in the **Parliament** and not in the state legislatures.
 
• This ensures uniformity throughout **India** regarding the nature of those fundamental rights and the punishment for their infringement.
 
 
 
• **Article 42:**
 
 
• This article is part of the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** under **Part IV**.
 
• It directs the **State** to make provisions for securing **just and humane conditions of work** and for **maternity relief**.
 
 
 
• **Article 45:**
 
 
• Originally, it provided for free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the **age of 14 years**.
 
• After the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, its scope was changed to provide **early childhood care and education** for all children until they complete the **age of six years**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Parliamentary Acts:** Under the powers of **Article 33**, the **Parliament** has enacted various legislations such as the **Army Act (1950)**, the **Navy Act (1950)**, the **Air Force Act (1950)**, the **Police Forces (Restriction of Rights) Act (1966)**, and the **Border Security Force Act**.
 
• **Restriction on Freedom:** These acts impose restrictions on their freedom of speech, right to form associations, right to be members of trade unions or political associations, and right to communicate with the press.
 
• **Court Martials:** **Article 33** also facilitates the exclusion of **court-martials** (tribunals established under military law) from the writ jurisdiction of the **Supreme Court** and the **High Courts** under **Article 32** and **Article 226** respectively, except where specified.
 
• **Public Order:** The mention of "forces entrusted with the maintenance of public order" specifically refers to **police forces** and **state armed police**, ensuring they remain neutral and disciplined during internal security duties.

questions.question: The process of fixing inorganic CO₂ into an organic form (sugar) is carried out in which of the following phases during photosynthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calvin-Benson cycle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of converting **inorganic carbon dioxide (CO₂)** into **organic compounds** like **sugar (glucose)** is known as **carbon fixation**, which occurs specifically during the **Calvin-Benson cycle**.
 
• This cycle is also referred to as the **light-independent phase** or the **dark reaction** of photosynthesis because it does not directly require light to proceed, although it depends on the products of the light-dependent reactions.
 
• The **Calvin-Benson cycle** takes place in the **stroma** of the **chloroplast**, the fluid-filled space surrounding the thylakoid membranes.
 
• It was discovered by **Melvin Calvin**, **Andrew Benson**, and **James Bassham** in **1950** at the **University of California, Berkeley**, using **radioactive carbon-14** to trace the path of carbon.
 
• The cycle utilizes the **chemical energy** stored in **ATP** and the **reducing power** of **NADPH**, both of which are generated during the **light-dependent phase**, to facilitate the synthesis of **hexose sugars**.
 
• The primary enzyme responsible for the first step of carbon fixation is **RuBisCO** (Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase), which is widely considered the most abundant **protein** on Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Light-dependent phase**:

 
 
• This phase occurs in the **thylakoid membranes** of the **chloroplast**.
 
• It involves the **absorption of light** by pigments like **chlorophyll a and b**, leading to the **photolysis of water** and the release of **oxygen** as a byproduct.
 
• The main function is to convert **solar energy** into **chemical energy** in the form of **ATP** and **NADPH**.
 
 
 
• **Glycolysis**:
 
 
• This is a **metabolic pathway** that occurs in the **cytoplasm** of the cell, not in the chloroplast.
 
• It is the first step of **cellular respiration** where one molecule of **glucose** (a 6-carbon sugar) is broken down into two molecules of **pyruvate** (a 3-carbon compound).
 
• It produces a net gain of **2 ATP** and **2 NADH** molecules and can occur in both **aerobic** and **anaerobic** conditions.
 
 
 
• **Kreb’s cycle**:
 
 
• Also known as the **Citric Acid Cycle** or **TCA cycle**, it occurs in the **matrix of the mitochondria**.
 
• It is part of **aerobic respiration** and involves the **oxidation of acetyl-CoA** derived from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins.
 
• The cycle releases **CO₂** as a waste product (the opposite of fixation) and generates high-energy carriers like **NADH** and **FADH₂** for the **electron transport chain**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Calvin Cycle** consists of **three main stages**:

 
 
• **Carbon Fixation**: **CO₂** binds with **Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP)** to form **3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA)**.
 
• **Reduction**: **ATP** and **NADPH** are used to convert **3-PGA** into **Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate (G3P)**, which is the precursor to **glucose**.
 
• **Regeneration**: Some **G3P** molecules are used to regenerate **RuBP** so the cycle can continue, requiring additional **ATP**.
 
 
 
• Plants that use only the **Calvin cycle** for carbon fixation are called **C3 plants** (e.g., **rice, wheat, soybeans**) because the first stable product is a **3-carbon molecule**.
 
• In **dry or hot environments**, some plants have evolved alternative pathways like **C4** (e.g., **maize, sugarcane**) or **CAM** (e.g., **cacti, pineapples**) to minimize **photorespiration** and conserve **water** while fixing carbon.

questions.question: LAN is often used in schools and offices. This abbreviation expands to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Local Area Network**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Local Area Network (LAN)** is a collection of devices connected together in one physical **location**, such as a **residence**, **office building**, **school**, or **university campus**.
 
• It is characterized by its **limited geographical range**, which typically spans from **100 meters to 2 kilometers**. Because of this small radius, **data transfer rates** are significantly higher, ranging from **10 Mbps to 10 Gbps**.
 
• **LANs** are usually **privately owned** by an organization or an individual, meaning the setup and maintenance are managed internally rather than by a public telecommunications provider.
 
• The primary **function** of a LAN is to facilitate **resource sharing** among users, such as sharing a single **printer**, **scanner**, **software applications**, or centralized **data storage**.
 
• Most modern LANs use **Ethernet** cables or **Wi-Fi** (Wireless LAN) for connectivity. The **IEEE 802.3** standard governs wired Ethernet, while **IEEE 802.11** governs wireless connections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Personal Area Network (PAN)**:

 
 
• This is the smallest type of network, typically used for communication among **personal devices** within a range of about **10 meters**.
 
• Common **examples** include connecting a **smartphone** to a **Bluetooth** headset or a **laptop** to a **wireless mouse**.
 
 
 
• **Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)**:
 
 
• A **MAN** covers a larger geographical **location** than a LAN but smaller than a WAN, such as an entire **city** or a large **campus**.
 
• It often connects multiple LANs within a city and is frequently used by **cable TV networks** or **Internet Service Providers (ISPs)** to provide city-wide connectivity.
 
 
 
• **Wide Area Network (WAN)**:
 
 
• A **WAN** extends over a large **geographical area**, such as a **country**, a **continent**, or the entire **globe**.
 
• The **Internet** is the most prominent **example** of a public WAN. It uses **satellites**, **fiber optic cables**, and **leased lines** for transmission.
 
 
 
• **Network Topologies**:
 
 
• LANs are often organized using specific layouts called **topologies**, such as **Star** (where all devices connect to a central **switch**), **Bus** (where devices share a single cable), and **Ring** (where devices are connected in a circle).
 
• The **Star topology** is the most common in modern **offices** because if one cable fails, the rest of the network remains functional.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hardware Components**: A LAN requires several **features** and hardware pieces to function, including **Network Interface Cards (NIC)**, **Hubs**, **Switches**, and **Routers**. A **Switch** is generally preferred over a Hub because it directs **data packets** specifically to the destination device, reducing **network congestion**.
 
• **Security**: Since LANs are private, they are generally more **secure** than public networks. However, they are still protected by **firewalls** and **encryption** protocols to prevent unauthorized access from the outside world.
 
• **WLAN (Wireless LAN)**: This is a type of LAN that uses **radio waves** instead of physical wires. It was revolutionized in the **year 1997** with the release of the first **802.11** standard, allowing for **mobility** within a **location**.
 
• **Cost and Maintenance**: The **initial cost** of setting up a LAN is relatively **low**. Because the **distance** is short, expensive **amplifiers** or **repeaters** are rarely needed, making it **cost-effective** for **small businesses** and **home users**.
